    import re
    from collections import defaultdict
    from pathlib import Path
    
    
    ROOT = Path("/tmp/liberty-run445-opaque-invisible-live")
    depth_clears = defaultdict(list)
    materializations = defaultdict(list)
    main_deferred = defaultdict(list)
    checkpoint_changes = defaultdict(list)
    
    for path in ROOT.glob("*.log"):
        for line in path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
            frame_match = re.search(r"frame=(\d+)", line)
            cmd_match = re.search(r"cmd=(\d+)", line)
            if not frame_match:
                continue
            frame = int(frame_match.group(1))
            cmd = int(cmd_match.group(1)) if cmd_match else None
            if "point=resolve-clear-applied" in line and "depth=true" in line:
                depth_clears[frame].append(cmd)
            if "point=depth-placement-view-materialized" in line:
                source_cmd = re.search(r"source-cmd=(\d+)", line)
                materializations[frame].append((cmd, int(source_cmd.group(1)) if source_cmd else None))
            if ("point=translucent-query-result" in line and
                    "category=deferred-light" in line and
                    "target=40076EB0/" in line):
                samples = re.search(r"samples-passed=(\d+)", line)
                stencil = re.search(r"stencil=(\d+)", line)
                main_deferred[frame].append(
                    (cmd, int(samples.group(1)), int(stencil.group(1)))
                )
            if "gta4-native-scene-checkpoint:" in line and "stage=scene-write-checkpoint" in line:
                checkpoint = re.search(r"checkpoint=(\d+)/", line)
                checksum = re.search(r"checksum=([0-9A-F]+)", line)
                if checkpoint and checksum:
                    checkpoint_changes[frame].append((int(checkpoint.group(1)), checksum.group(1)))
    
    joined = []
    for frame in sorted(set(depth_clears) & set(materializations) & set(main_deferred)):
        clear_commands = set(depth_clears[frame])
        copied_clear = any(source_cmd in clear_commands for _, source_cmd in materializations[frame])
        stencil_queries = [entry for entry in main_deferred[frame] if entry[2] == 1]
        zero_stencil_queries = sum(samples == 0 for _, samples, _ in stencil_queries)
        joined.append((frame, copied_clear, len(stencil_queries), zero_stencil_queries))
    
    print("joined_frames", len(joined))
    print("frames_copying_same_frame_depth_clear", sum(entry[1] for entry in joined))
    print("stencil_queries", sum(entry[2] for entry in joined))
    print("zero_stencil_queries", sum(entry[3] for entry in joined))

**Outlining EDRAM clear range fix approach**

## Assistant

The execution logs expose the root cause: the new resolve-clear implementation violates Xenos EDRAM overlap semantics.

At frame 6720:

- Resolve command 1870 requests simultaneous color and depth clears.
- Native code clears the entire color image and the entire depth/stencil image independently. [run 445 log](</tmp/liberty-run445-opaque-invisible-live/Liberty Recompiled_445.8.log:4815>)
- Command 1876 then materializes that fully cleared 2× depth/stencil image into the 1× deferred attachment. [run 445 log](</tmp/liberty-run445-opaque-invisible-live/Liberty Recompiled_445.8.log:4863>)
- The first main deferred pass requires stencil equal to `1`, but the copied stencil is `0`, so it passes zero samples. [run 445 log](</tmp/liberty-run445-opaque-invisible-live/Liberty Recompiled_445.8.log:7427>)
- The main target remains exactly black through checkpoint 38. Checkpoint 39 is the sky pass, which finally changes it. [run 445 log](</tmp/liberty-run445-opaque-invisible-live/Liberty Recompiled_445.8.log:7203>)

That exactly matches the screenshots: deferred geometry is absent, while sky, credits, emissives, and unmasked lights remain.

Why the clear is wrong:

The established EDRAM cache explicitly prevents simultaneous color and depth clear ranges from overlapping because they occupy the same circular 2048-tile EDRAM. [cache.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/pipeline/render_target/cache.cpp:1052)

For the live descriptors—2× MSAA, pitch 80, depth base 0, color base 1—the verified calculation gives:

- Color clear: 2047 EDRAM tiles.
- Depth/stencil clear: only 1 tile.
- Current native implementation: clears the entire depth/stencil Vulkan image.

The result is identical using either the guest or native-resolution dimensions because both spans exceed the 2048-tile circular EDRAM range.

The faulty implementation is [graphics_system.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/gta4_native/graphics_system.cpp:8826). It executes two independent full-image `vkCmdClearAttachments` operations and marks each whole surface as the newest owner. It has no circular tile-range calculation or color/depth overlap exclusion.

This repeats consistently: across 28 joined captured frames, every depth materialization selected the same-frame over-broad resolve clear. Of 891 main stencil-dependent deferred queries, 803 passed zero samples.

The rejected command 1875 is not the cause: it requests depth function `Never`, no depth write, and no stencil write. It could not rebuild the missing stencil mask even if recorded.

The proper fix is range-aware resolve clearing:

- Calculate guest EDRAM tile ranges from the resolve rectangle, pitch, MSAA layout, format width, and original color/depth bases.
- Apply circular 2048-tile wrapping.
- Clip simultaneous color/depth clears so their ownership ranges never overlap, matching the established cache.
- Clear and claim only those ranges—not the complete Vulkan surfaces.
- Preserve unaffected depth/stencil content when materializing 2× → 1× views.
- Add logs containing unclipped/clipped tile starts and lengths, wrapped bases, and resulting alias ownership.

This should not be patched by disabling depth clears or special-casing deferred lighting. The defect is the missing EDRAM range-ownership semantics in `RecordResolveClears`.

- `StretchRect` records an explicit surface-to-texture copy. [video.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/Reference%20Projects/UnleashedRecomp-main/UnleashedRecomp/gpu/video.cpp:3265)

- Clears happen only through the high-level hooked `Clear` operation, after pending copies are completed. [video.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/Reference%20Projects/UnleashedRecomp-main/UnleashedRecomp/gpu/video.cpp:3676)

Then the placement-alias system propagates that mutation into a different native depth surface. Neither mechanism follows Unleashed’s native model.

The corrected research direction is:

- Track GTA surface objects and explicit copy/resolve relationships.
- Resolve MSAA using those relationships.
- Preserve source content until an actual high-level clear command targets that surface.
- Stop using placement addresses to infer cross-surface ownership.
- Remove raw resolve-bit-driven clearing from the native resource path unless the title hook translates it into a deliberate native clear operation with the correct surface identity and ordering.

    from pathlib import Path
    import re
    
    ROOT = Path('/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/gta4-recomp/generated')
    TARGETS = ('sub_82A3CC68(ctx, base);', 'sub_82A3EDA8(ctx, base);')
    
    for path in sorted(ROOT.glob('gta4_recomp.*.cpp')):
        lines = path.read_text(errors='replace').splitlines()
        current = None
        start = None
        for index, line in enumerate(lines):
            match = re.match(r'DEFINE_REX_FUNC\(([^)]+)\)', line)
            if match:
                current = match.group(1)
                start = index
            if not any(target in line for target in TARGETS):
                continue
            lo = max(start if start is not None else 0, index - 42)
            hi = min(len(lines), index + 8)
            print(f'\n=== {path.name}:{index + 1} caller={current} function_start={(start + 1) if start is not None else 0} ===')
            for out_index in range(lo, hi):
                print(f'{out_index + 1}: {lines[out_index]}')

    +bool Gta4NativeGraphicsSystem::RecordDepthStencilDiagnosticProbe(
    +    VkCommandBuffer command_buffer, NativeSurfaceImage& image,
    +    uint8_t depth_kind, uint8_t stencil_kind) {
    +  if (!ShouldLogDiagnosticFrame(diagnostic_submitted_frame_) ||
    +      !(image.aspect & VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_DEPTH_BIT) ||
    +      !(image.aspect & VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_STENCIL_BIT) ||
    +      !InitializeContentProbeBuffer()) {
    +    return false;
    +  }
    +  if (content_probe_buffer_.pending_frame != diagnostic_submitted_frame_) {
    +    std::memset(content_probe_buffer_.mapping, 0, size_t(kContentProbeBufferSize));
    +    content_probe_buffer_.pending_frame = diagnostic_submitted_frame_;
    +    content_probe_buffer_.stages = {};
    +  }
    +  uint32_t depth_stage = 0;
    +  while (depth_stage < content_probe_buffer_.stages.size() &&
    +         content_probe_buffer_.stages[depth_stage].valid) {
    +    ++depth_stage;
    +  }
    +  const uint32_t stencil_stage = depth_stage + 1;
    +  if (stencil_stage >= content_probe_buffer_.stages.size()) {
    +    return false;
    +  }
    +  const bool depth_recorded = RecordContentProbeImage(
    +      command_buffer, depth_stage, image.resource.image, image.format, image.layout,
    +      image.width, image.height, image.descriptor.handle, image.descriptor.address,
    +      depth_kind, 0, VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_DEPTH_BIT);
    +  const bool stencil_recorded = RecordContentProbeImage(
    +      command_buffer, stencil_stage, image.resource.image, image.format, image.layout,
    +      image.width, image.height, image.descriptor.handle, image.descriptor.address,
    +      stencil_kind, 0, VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_STENCIL_BIT);
    +  if (depth_recorded) {
    +    content_probe_buffer_.stages[depth_stage].command_index =
    +        uint32_t(diagnostic_command_index_);
    +  }
    +  if (stencil_recorded) {
    +    content_probe_buffer_.stages[stencil_stage].command_index =
    +        uint32_t(diagnostic_command_index_);
    +  }
    +  return depth_recorded && stencil_recorded;
    +}

    from pathlib import Path
    import re
    
    log_path = Path(
        "/tmp/liberty-run455-wrapper-evidence.wXeyoa/Liberty Recompiled_455.log"
    )
    lines = log_path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
    
    frame = 4080
    resolve_command = 306
    bind_command = 314
    
    resolve_records = []
    bind_records = []
    materialization_records = []
    
    for line_number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        if f"frame={frame}" not in line:
            continue
        if f"cmd={resolve_command}" in line and "point=resolve-begin" in line:
            resolve_records.append((line_number, line))
        if f"cmd={bind_command}" in line and "point=depth-bind-transition" in line:
            bind_records.append((line_number, line))
        if f"cmd={bind_command}" in line and "point=depth-placement-view-materialized" in line:
            materialization_records.append((line_number, line))
    
    def extract(pattern: str, line: str) -> str:
        match = re.search(pattern, line)
        if not match:
            raise RuntimeError(f"missing pattern {pattern!r} in {line!r}")
        return match.group(1)
    
    resolve_line = resolve_records[0][1]
    bind_line = bind_records[0][1]
    materialization_line = materialization_records[0][1]
    
    resolve_owner = extract(r" owner=([0-9A-F]{8})", resolve_line)
    resolve_source = extract(r" source=([0-9A-F]{8})", resolve_line)
    primary_wrapper = extract(r" wrapper=([0-9A-F]{8})", bind_line)
    primary_surface = extract(r" surface=([0-9A-F]{8})/", bind_line)
    materialized_source = extract(r" source=([0-9A-F]{8})/", materialization_line)
    materialized_destination = extract(r" destination=([0-9A-F]{8})/", materialization_line)
    
    print(f"log={log_path}")
    print(f"resolve_records={len(resolve_records)}")
    print(f"bind_records={len(bind_records)}")
    print(f"materialization_records={len(materialization_records)}")
    print(f"resolve_line={resolve_records[0][0]}")
    print(f"bind_line={bind_records[0][0]}")
    print(f"materialization_line={materialization_records[0][0]}")
    print(f"resolve_owner={resolve_owner}")
    print(f"resolve_source={resolve_source}")
    print(f"primary_wrapper={primary_wrapper}")
    print(f"primary_surface={primary_surface}")
    print(f"materialized_source={materialized_source}")
    print(f"materialized_destination={materialized_destination}")
    print(f"wrappers_distinct={resolve_owner != primary_wrapper}")

        "materializer_join_matches="
        f"{materialized_source == resolve_source and materialized_destination == primary_surface}"

- Before the incorrect handoff, all 256 sampled primary-stencil points contain `6`. [Log line 1369](</tmp/liberty-run455-wrapper-evidence.wXeyoa/Liberty Recompiled_455.frame4080.log:1369>)
- Afterward, all sampled points are zero. [Log line 1371](</tmp/liberty-run455-wrapper-evidence.wXeyoa/Liberty Recompiled_455.frame4080.log:1371>)
- The next composite requires stencil `Equal`, reference `1`, mask `1`, and gets zero surviving samples. [Log line 1489](</tmp/liberty-run455-wrapper-evidence.wXeyoa/Liberty Recompiled_455.frame4080.log:1489>)

The responsible code scans all placement owners for a descriptor-compatible depth source, regardless of guest object identity: [graphics_system.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/gta4_native/graphics_system.cpp:8583). It then duplicates the depth resolve attachment into the stencil attachment and resolves both: [graphics_system.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/gta4_native/graphics_system.cpp:8876). `PrepareSurfaceContent` triggers that automatically during binding: [graphics_system.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src/graphics/gta4_native/graphics_system.cpp:9034).

Unleashed does not do this. It creates one native texture per explicit surface object, binds explicit object pointers, and only associates resources through an explicit `StretchRect` operation: [video.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/Reference%20Projects/UnleashedRecomp-main/UnleashedRecomp/gpu/video.cpp:3184), [video.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/Reference%20Projects/UnleashedRecomp-main/UnleashedRecomp/gpu/video.cpp:3253), [video.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/Reference%20Projects/UnleashedRecomp-main/UnleashedRecomp/gpu/video.cpp:3346).

Therefore:

- The title clear flags are not wrong.
- The explicit deferred resolve is not corrupting stencil.
- The stencil writers are not failing.
- The alpha-test correction is not causing this regression.
- The automatic cross-object “placement view” materializer is the fault.

The architecturally correct fix is to remove this inferred cross-object handoff and preserve native surface identity. Any required deferred-to-forward depth transfer must come from an explicit title-level relationship, and should preserve the primary surface’s independent stencil lifecycle. The device supports depth-only resolve with stencil resolve set to `NONE`, as permitted by Vulkan when `independentResolveNone` is true. [Khronos documentation](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkPhysicalDeviceDepthStencilResolveProperties.html)

No behavior fix was implemented during this research pass. The instrumentation build succeeded, the evidence is preserved, and no Git operations were used.

Yes. I regressed it.

Run 465—the build you saw working—rejected the handoff, so it never mutated the primary depth/stencil image. Run 466 wired the real `40226690` source and began executing; its independent probes show destination stencil changing from `6` before the handoff to `0` after it. That is exactly when the scene disappeared.

The mistake is narrower than the source selection: I used combined D32S8 views for an operation intended to resolve only depth. The renderer already owns depth-aspect-only views for both surfaces. I’m switching this explicit handoff to those views and making the test require the stencil checksum to remain identical. No EDRAM model and no generic resource scan.

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import collections
    import glob
    import re
    import sys
    
    
    FIELD_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^| )([a-z][a-z-]*)=([^ ]+)")
    FOCUS = {
        "water-surface",
        "vehicle-glass",
        "vehicle-light",
        "glass",
        "light-sprite",
        "emissive",
        "alpha-reflect",
    }
    
    
    def parse_run(pattern: str):
        rows = []
        files = sorted(glob.glob(pattern))
        for path in files:
            with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as handle:
                for line_number, line in enumerate(handle, 1):
                    if "point=translucent-query-result" not in line:
                        continue
                    fields = dict(FIELD_RE.findall(line))
                    fields["path"] = path
                    fields["line"] = str(line_number)
                    rows.append(fields)
        return files, rows
    
    
    def summarize(label: str, rows):
        print(f"RUN {label}: query_rows={len(rows)}")
        counts = collections.defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0, 0])
        primary = collections.defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0, 0])
        for row in rows:
            category = row.get("category", "?")
            variant = row.get("variant", "?")
            samples = int(row.get("samples-passed", "0"), 0)
            key = (category, variant)
            counts[key][0] += 1
            counts[key][1 if samples == 0 else 2] += 1
            if row.get("depth", "").startswith("400007C0/"):
                primary[key][0] += 1
                primary[key][1 if samples == 0 else 2] += 1
    
        categories = sorted({key[0] for key in counts if key[0] in FOCUS})
        for category in categories:
            print(f"  category={category}")
            for variant in ("original", "depth-only", "stencil-only", "raster-only"):
                total, zero, nonzero = counts[(category, variant)]
                ptotal, pzero, pnonzero = primary[(category, variant)]
                if total:
                    print(
                        f"    {variant:12s} all={total}:zero={zero}:nonzero={nonzero} "
                        f"primary={ptotal}:zero={pzero}:nonzero={pnonzero}"
                    )
    
    
    def main() -> int:
        if len(sys.argv) != 3:
            raise SystemExit("usage: compare_translucent_runs.py RUN465_GLOB RUN470_GLOB")
        for label, pattern in (("465", sys.argv[1]), ("470", sys.argv[2])):
            files, rows = parse_run(pattern)
            print(f"FILES {label}: {len(files)}")
            summarize(label, rows)
        return 0
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        raise SystemExit(main())

    +bool Gta4NativeGraphicsSystem::EnsureDepthHandoffStencilScratch(
    +    NativeSurfaceImage& destination) {
    +  if (destination.depth_handoff_stencil_scratch.image) {
    +    return true;
    +  }
    +
    +  auto* vulkan_provider =
    +      static_cast<ui::vulkan::VulkanProvider*>(provider_.get());
    +  const ui::vulkan::VulkanDevice* vulkan_device =
    +      vulkan_provider ? vulkan_provider->vulkan_device() : nullptr;
    +  if (!vulkan_device) {
    +    return false;
    +  }
    +
    +  VkImageCreateInfo image_info{};
    +  image_info.sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_IMAGE_CREATE_INFO;
    +  image_info.imageType = VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D;
    +  image_info.format = destination.format;
    +  image_info.extent = {destination.width, destination.height, 1};
    +  image_info.mipLevels = 1;
    +  image_info.arrayLayers = 1;
    +  image_info.samples = VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT;
    +  image_info.tiling = VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL;
    +  image_info.usage =
    +      VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT | VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT;
    +  image_info.sharingMode = VK_SHARING_MODE_EXCLUSIVE;
    +  image_info.initialLayout = VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED;
    +  if (!ui::vulkan::util::CreateDedicatedAllocationImage(
    +          vulkan_device, image_info,
    +          ui::vulkan::util::MemoryPurpose::kDeviceLocal,
    +          destination.depth_handoff_stencil_scratch.image,
    +          destination.depth_handoff_stencil_scratch.memory)) {

    +    destination.depth_handoff_stencil_scratch_layout =
    +        VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED;
    +    return false;
    +  }
    +
    +  destination.depth_handoff_stencil_scratch_layout =
    +      VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED;
    +  REXLOG_INFO(
    +      "gta4-native-cause: point=explicit-depth-handoff-stencil-scratch "
    +      "result=created destination={:08X}/{:08X} extent={}x{} format={}",
    +      destination.descriptor.handle, destination.descriptor.address,

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import glob
    import re
    import sys
    
    
    FIELD_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^| )([a-z][a-z-]*)=([^ ]+)")
    STAGES = {
        "stencil-explicit-handoff-destination-before": "stencil-before",
        "stencil-explicit-handoff-destination-after": "stencil-after",
        "depth-explicit-handoff-destination-before": "depth-before",
        "depth-explicit-handoff-destination-after": "depth-after",
    }
    
    
    def main() -> int:
        if len(sys.argv) != 2:
            raise SystemExit("usage: analyze_handoff_invariants.py LOG_GLOB")
        values = {}
        for path in sorted(glob.glob(sys.argv[1])):
            with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as handle:
                for line_number, line in enumerate(handle, 1):
                    if "explicit-handoff-destination" not in line:
                        continue
                    fields = dict(FIELD_RE.findall(line))
                    stage = fields.get("stage")
                    if stage not in STAGES:
                        continue
                    key = (fields.get("frame"), fields.get("cmd"))
                    values.setdefault(key, {})[STAGES[stage]] = {
                        "checksum": fields.get("checksum"),
                        "min": fields.get("min"),
                        "max": fields.get("max"),
                        "path": path,
                        "line": line_number,
                    }
    
        stencil_pairs = []
        depth_pairs = []
        for key, record in sorted(values.items(), key=lambda item: tuple(int(v) for v in item[0])):
            if "stencil-before" in record and "stencil-after" in record:
                stencil_pairs.append((key, record))
            if "depth-before" in record and "depth-after" in record:
                depth_pairs.append((key, record))
    
        stencil_mismatches = [
            (key, record)
            for key, record in stencil_pairs
            if record["stencil-before"]["checksum"] != record["stencil-after"]["checksum"]
        ]
        depth_changes = [
            (key, record)
            for key, record in depth_pairs
            if record["depth-before"]["checksum"] != record["depth-after"]["checksum"]
        ]
        print(
            f"stencil_pairs={len(stencil_pairs)} "
            f"stencil_mismatches={len(stencil_mismatches)}"
        )
        print(f"depth_pairs={len(depth_pairs)} depth_changes={len(depth_changes)}")
        for label, rows in (
            ("stencil-mismatch", stencil_mismatches[:10]),
            ("depth-change", depth_changes[:10]),
        ):
            for key, record in rows:
                before = record[label.split("-")[0] + "-before"]
                after = record[label.split("-")[0] + "-after"]
                print(
                    f"{label} frame={key[0]} cmd={key[1]} "
                    f"before={before['checksum']}:{before['min']}:{before['max']} "
                    f"after={after['checksum']}:{after['min']}:{after['max']} "
                    f"at={after['path']}:{after['line']}"
                )
        nonzero_stencil = [
            (key, record)
            for key, record in stencil_pairs
            if record["stencil-before"].get("max") not in (None, "0")
        ]
        print(f"nonzero_stencil_pairs={len(nonzero_stencil)}")
        for key, record in nonzero_stencil[:10]:
            before = record["stencil-before"]
            after = record["stencil-after"]
            print(
                f"nonzero-stencil frame={key[0]} cmd={key[1]} "
                f"before={before['checksum']}:{before['min']}:{before['max']} "
                f"after={after['checksum']}:{after['min']}:{after['max']}"
            )
        return 0
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        raise SystemExit(main())

## Assistant

The new 472 capture explains the last loop precisely. Combined views do transfer depth, but MoltenVK’s stencil-aspect image-to-image restore also restores the combined Metal texture’s depth plane—so it puts depth `1` back after the resolve. That is why both before/after probes stay `1` even though the title source is `0`.

I’m changing only the preservation transport: stencil image → byte buffer → stencil image. The existing stencil probes already use image-to-buffer and prove MoltenVK exposes stencil independently that way. This keeps the combined-view depth resolve, preserves stencil without a combined image blit, and avoids any guest-memory or EDRAM behavior.

## Assistant

The actual fix was:

- Use the title’s explicit resolved depth texture `D9132320` as the handoff source.
- Copy only its depth aspect into forward depth surface `400007C0`.
- Preserve `400007C0`’s stencil through the existing buffer transport.
- Stop copying the cleared MSAA attachment `40226690`.
- No EDRAM aliasing, placement scan, or alpha changes.

Run 481 proves it. In frame 3720, the depth checksum is identical across:

`D9132320 after resolve → handoff source → 400007C0 → first opaque consumer → first translucent consumer`

All five equal `2630559647D3302A`. The stencil checksum also remains identical across the handoff and both consumers.

The additional edits were diagnostic instrumentation:

- Selected the first opaque draw using `400007C0`.
- Selected the first water/glass/light draw using `400007C0`.
- Probed depth/stencil before both.
- Captured RT0 checksums before and after both draws.
- Added wrapper, handle, generation, sample-count, frame/command, and provenance fields.
- Traced `40226690` before/after its clear and `D9132320` immediately after the explicit resolve.

I was trying to prove opaque and translucent rendering simultaneously—not fix another renderer subsystem. The RT0 sparse probes still need refinement because the selected sample grid can miss a small draw even when it renders.

Important: the working game is using the successfully built 11:06 binary containing the `D9132320 → 400007C0` fix. Afterward, I started backing that fix out to obey the “research first” instruction, but that rollback never compiled. The current source is partially reverted and does not match the working binary, so it must be restored to the 11:06 implementation before another rebuild.

        "explicit-title-resolve-destination-after",
        "explicit-resolved-handoff-source",
        "forward-phase-entry",
        "first-opaque-consumer-before",
        "first-translucent-consumer-before",
    }
    
    depth_by_frame = defaultdict(dict)
    stencil_by_frame = defaultdict(dict)
    query_passes = defaultdict(int)
    query_totals = defaultdict(int)
    errors = []
    
    depth_pattern = re.compile(
        r"point=depth-lifecycle-value frame=(\d+).*?role=([^ ]+).*?"
        r"aspect=2 .*?min=([^ ]+) max=([^ ]+).*?checksum=([0-9A-F]+)"
    )
    stencil_pattern = re.compile(
        r"point=depth-lifecycle-value frame=(\d+).*?role=([^ ]+).*?"
        r"aspect=stencil .*?checksum=([0-9A-F]+)"
    )
    query_pattern = re.compile(
        r"point=translucent-query-result .*?category=([^ ]+) variant=original .*?"
        r"samples-passed=(\d+)"
    )
    
    for path in sorted(LOG_DIR.glob("Liberty Recompiled_488*.log")):
        for line in path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
            if any(token in line for token in ("Validation Error", "VUID-", "device lost", "Device lost")):
                errors.append((path.name, line))
            depth_match = depth_pattern.search(line)
            if depth_match and depth_match.group(2) in ROLES:
                frame = int(depth_match.group(1))
                depth_by_frame[frame][depth_match.group(2)] = {
                    "minimum": Decimal(depth_match.group(3)),
                    "maximum": Decimal(depth_match.group(4)),
                    "checksum": depth_match.group(5),
                }
            stencil_match = stencil_pattern.search(line)
            if stencil_match and stencil_match.group(2) in ROLES:
                frame = int(stencil_match.group(1))
                stencil_by_frame[frame][stencil_match.group(2)] = stencil_match.group(3)
            query_match = query_pattern.search(line)
            if query_match:
                category = query_match.group(1)
                query_totals[category] += 1
                if int(query_match.group(2)) > 0:
                    query_passes[category] += 1
    
    complete_frames = sorted(
        frame
        for frame, values in depth_by_frame.items()
        if set(values) == ROLES and set(stencil_by_frame[frame]) == ROLES
    )
    if not complete_frames:
        raise SystemExit("no complete joined lifecycle frame")
    
    frame = complete_frames[-1]
    depth_values = depth_by_frame[frame]
    depth_checksums = {value["checksum"] for value in depth_values.values()}
    stencil_checksums = set(stencil_by_frame[frame].values())
    noncleared = all(
        value["minimum"] > Decimal(0) and value["maximum"] > value["minimum"]
        for value in depth_values.values()
    )
    
    print("frame", frame)
    for role in sorted(ROLES):
        value = depth_values[role]
        print(
            role,
            "depth",
            value["checksum"],
            "min",
            value["minimum"],
            "max",
            value["maximum"],
            "stencil",
            stencil_by_frame[frame][role],
        )
    print("depth-all-equal", len(depth_checksums) == 1)
    print("stencil-all-equal", len(stencil_checksums) == 1)
    print("depth-noncleared-and-nonuniform", noncleared)
    for category in ("water-surface", "vehicle-glass", "vehicle-light", "light-sprite"):
        print(
            "query",
            category,
            "passed",
            query_passes[category],
            "total",
            query_totals[category],
        )
    print("validation-or-device-loss-errors", len(errors))
    
    if len(depth_checksums) != 1 or len(stencil_checksums) != 1 or not noncleared or errors:
        raise SystemExit(1)

    raw = git_bytes("ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "-z")

    }

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import glob
    import math
    import re
    import statistics
    from collections import defaultdict
    
    BASE = "/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/out/build/macos-release/LibertyRecomp/Liberty Recompiled.app/Contents/MacOS/logs/Liberty Recompiled_477*.log"
    MARKER = "gta4-native-perf: "
    FIELD = re.compile(r"([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)=([^\s]+)")
    
    records = []
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(BASE)):
        with open(path, "rt", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as source:
            for line_number, line in enumerate(source, 1):
                pos = line.find(MARKER)
                if pos < 0:
                    continue
                record = dict(FIELD.findall(line[pos + len(MARKER):]))
                record["_path"] = path
                record["_line"] = line_number
                records.append(record)
    
    def f(record, key):
        return float(record.get(key, "0"))
    
    def i(record, key):
        return int(record.get(key, "0"))
    
    def percentile(values, p):
        ordered = sorted(values)
        if not ordered:
            return math.nan
        rank = (len(ordered) - 1) * p
        low = math.floor(rank)
        high = math.ceil(rank)
        if low == high:
            return ordered[low]
        return ordered[low] * (high - rank) + ordered[high] * (rank - low)
    
    def describe(label, values):
        if not values:
            print(f"{label}: n=0")
            return
        print(
            f"{label}: n={len(values)} mean={statistics.fmean(values):.6f} "
            f"p50={percentile(values, 0.50):.6f} p95={percentile(values, 0.95):.6f} "
            f"p99={percentile(values, 0.99):.6f} max={max(values):.6f} "
            f"stdev={statistics.pstdev(values):.6f}"
        )
    
    frames = [record for record in records if record.get("point") == "frame"]
    frames.sort(key=lambda record: i(record, "frame"))
    print(f"records={len(records)} frames={len(frames)}")
    for metric in (
        "gpu-ms", "cpu-callback-ms", "cpu-wait-ms", "cpu-texture-ms",
        "cpu-record-ms", "cpu-submit-ms", "upload-bytes"
    ):
        describe(metric, [f(record, metric) for record in frames])
    
    gameplay = [record for record in frames if i(record, "resident[pipelines") >= 50]
    print(f"gameplay-cutoff-resident-pipelines>=50 count={len(gameplay)}")
    for metric in ("gpu-ms", "cpu-wait-ms", "cpu-texture-ms", "cpu-record-ms", "cpu-submit-ms", "upload-bytes"):
        describe(f"gameplay-{metric}", [f(record, metric) for record in gameplay])
    
    scopes_by_frame = defaultdict(list)
    for record in records:
        if record.get("point") == "scope":
            scopes_by_frame[i(record, "frame")].append(record)
    
    for frame in frames:
        fid = i(frame, "frame")
        phases = scopes_by_frame[fid]
        main_unknown = sum(f(scope, "gpu-ms") for scope in phases if scope.get("kind") == "render-phase" and scope.get("phase") == "unknown")
        composite = sum(f(scope, "gpu-ms") for scope in phases if scope.get("kind") == "render-phase" and scope.get("phase") == "composite-postfx")
        present = sum(f(scope, "gpu-ms") for scope in phases if scope.get("kind") == "present")
        print(
            f"frame={fid} gpu={f(frame,'gpu-ms'):.6f} unknown={main_unknown:.6f} "
            f"composite={composite:.6f} present={present:.6f} "
            f"upload={f(frame,'upload-bytes'):.0f} textures={frame.get('created[pipelines','?')} "
            f"source={frame['_path']}:{frame['_line']}"
        )
    
    def pearson(xs, ys):
        if len(xs) != len(ys) or len(xs) < 2:
            return math.nan
        mx = statistics.fmean(xs)
        my = statistics.fmean(ys)
        numerator = sum((x - mx) * (y - my) for x, y in zip(xs, ys))
        denominator = math.sqrt(sum((x - mx) ** 2 for x in xs) * sum((y - my) ** 2 for y in ys))
        return numerator / denominator if denominator else math.nan
    
    gpu = [f(record, "gpu-ms") for record in frames]
    for metric in ("upload-bytes", "cpu-texture-ms", "cpu-record-ms", "cpu-submit-ms", "cpu-wait-ms"):
        print(f"pearson-gpu-vs-{metric}={pearson(gpu, [f(record, metric) for record in frames]):.6f}")

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import glob
    import math
    import re
    import statistics
    from collections import Counter, defaultdict
    
    LOGS = "/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/out/build/macos-release/LibertyRecomp/Liberty Recompiled.app/Contents/MacOS/logs/Liberty Recompiled_474*.log"
    FRAME_RE = re.compile(r"point=frame frame=(\d+).*?gpu-ms=([0-9.]+).*?cpu-wait-ms=([0-9.]+)")
    QUERY_BEGIN_RE = re.compile(r"point=translucent-query-frame-begin frame=(\d+)")
    QUERY_RECORDED_RE = re.compile(r"point=translucent-query-recorded frame=(\d+).*?variant=([^\s]+)")
    QUERY_RESULT_RE = re.compile(r"point=translucent-query-result frame=(\d+).*?variant=([^\s]+)")
    CONTENT_RE = re.compile(r"point=([^\s]*content[^\s]*probe[^\s]*) frame=(\d+)")
    
    profile = {}
    trace_frames = set()
    recorded = defaultdict(Counter)
    results = defaultdict(Counter)
    content = defaultdict(Counter)
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(LOGS)):
        with open(path, "rt", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as source:
            for line in source:
                match = FRAME_RE.search(line)
                if match:
                    profile[int(match.group(1))] = (float(match.group(2)), float(match.group(3)))
                match = QUERY_BEGIN_RE.search(line)
                if match:
                    trace_frames.add(int(match.group(1)))
                match = QUERY_RECORDED_RE.search(line)
                if match:
                    recorded[int(match.group(1))][match.group(2)] += 1
                match = QUERY_RESULT_RE.search(line)
                if match:
                    results[int(match.group(1))][match.group(2)] += 1
                match = CONTENT_RE.search(line)
                if match:
                    content[int(match.group(2))][match.group(1)] += 1
    
    rows = []
    for traced in sorted(trace_frames):
        following = traced + 1
        if following not in profile:
            continue
        gpu, wait = profile[following]
        rec = recorded[traced]
        res = results[traced]
        extra = sum(value for variant, value in rec.items() if variant != "original")
        originals = rec["original"]
        rows.append((traced, following, gpu, wait, originals, extra, sum(rec.values()), sum(content[traced].values())))
    
    for row in rows:
        print(
            "trace-frame={} profile-frame={} gpu-ms={:.6f} prior-frame-wait-ms={:.6f} "
            "original-queries={} replay-draws={} total-queries={} content-probe-records={}".format(*row)
        )
    
    def percentile(values, p):
        ordered = sorted(values)
        rank = (len(ordered) - 1) * p
        low = math.floor(rank)
        high = math.ceil(rank)
        return ordered[low] if low == high else ordered[low] * (high - rank) + ordered[high] * (rank - low)
    
    for column, label in ((2, "gpu-ms"), (3, "prior-frame-wait-ms"), (4, "original-queries"), (5, "replay-draws"), (6, "total-queries"), (7, "content-probe-records")):
        values = [row[column] for row in rows]
        if values:
            print(
                f"{label}: n={len(values)} mean={statistics.fmean(values):.6f} "
                f"p50={percentile(values, 0.50):.6f} p95={percentile(values, 0.95):.6f} "
                f"p99={percentile(values, 0.99):.6f} max={max(values):.6f}"

    QUERY_RECORDED = re.compile(r"point=translucent-query-recorded frame=(\d+).*?category=([^\s]+) variant=([^\s]+)")
    QUERY_RESULT = re.compile(r"point=translucent-query-result frame=(\d+).*?category=([^\s]+) variant=([^\s]+)")
    CAUSE_FRAME = re.compile(r"gta4-native-cause: point=([^\s]+) frame=(\d+)")
    FRAME_BEGIN = re.compile(r"\[NativeTrace\] frame=(\d+).*?point=frame-begin commands=(\d+)")
    
    points = defaultdict(Counter)
    query_recorded = defaultdict(Counter)
    query_results = defaultdict(Counter)
    causes = defaultdict(Counter)
    commands = {}
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(LOGS)):
        with open(path, "rt", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as source:
            for line in source:
                match = FRAME_BEGIN.search(line)
                if match:
                    commands[int(match.group(1))] = int(match.group(2))
                match = NATIVE.search(line)
                if match:
                    points[int(match.group(1))][match.group(2)] += 1
                match = QUERY_RECORDED.search(line)
                if match:
                    query_recorded[int(match.group(1))][(match.group(2), match.group(3))] += 1
                match = QUERY_RESULT.search(line)
                if match:
                    query_results[int(match.group(1))][(match.group(2), match.group(3))] += 1
                match = CAUSE_FRAME.search(line)
                if match:
                    causes[int(match.group(2))][match.group(1)] += 1
    
    frames = sorted(set(points) | set(query_recorded) | set(query_results) | set(causes) | set(commands))
    for frame in frames:
        if not (frame <= 4 or frame % 120 == 0):
            continue
        rec = query_recorded[frame]
        original = sum(count for (category, variant), count in rec.items() if variant == "original")
        replay = sum(count for (category, variant), count in rec.items() if variant != "original")
        probe_causes = sum(count for point, count in causes[frame].items() if "probe" in point)
        print(
            f"frame={frame} queued={commands.get(frame, 0)} native-events={sum(points[frame].values())} "
            f"command-begin={points[frame]['command-begin']} rendering-begin={points[frame]['rendering-begin']} "
            f"queries-original={original} replay-draws={replay} query-total={sum(rec.values())} "
            f"cause-probe-events={probe_causes}"
        )
        print("  query-categories=" + ",".join(f"{category}/{variant}:{count}" for (category, variant), count in sorted(rec.items())))
        interesting = {key: value for key, value in causes[frame].items() if "probe" in key or "pipeline" in key or "texture" in key}
        print("  cause=" + ",".join(f"{key}:{value}" for key, value in sorted(interesting.items())))

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import collections
    import glob
    import re
    
    LOG_GLOB = "/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/out/build/macos-release/LibertyRecomp/Liberty Recompiled.app/Contents/MacOS/logs/Liberty Recompiled_491*.log"
    FRAMES = {3240, 3360, 3480, 3600, 3720}
    
    field_re = re.compile(r"\b(frame|cmd|vs|ps|rt|depth|blend|alpha|z|stencil|color-mask)=([^ ]+)")
    
    rows = []
    for path in glob.glob(LOG_GLOB):
        with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as handle:
            for line in handle:
                if "point=draw-state" not in line:
                    continue
                fields = dict(field_re.findall(line))
                if not fields or int(fields["frame"]) not in FRAMES:
                    continue
                blend = int(fields["blend"].split(":", 1)[0])
                alpha = int(fields["alpha"].split(":", 1)[0])
                rt = fields["rt"].split(":", 1)[0]
                depth = fields["depth"].split(":", 1)[0]
                vs_parts = fields["vs"].split(":")
                ps_parts = fields["ps"].split(":")
                vs_hash = vs_parts[-1]
                ps_hash = ps_parts[-1]
                mode = "blend" if blend else ("alpha" if alpha else "opaque")
                rows.append({
                    "frame": int(fields["frame"]),
                    "cmd": int(fields["cmd"]),
                    "mode": mode,
                    "blend": blend,
                    "alpha": alpha,
                    "rt": rt,
                    "depth": depth,
                    "vs": vs_hash,
                    "ps": ps_hash,
                    "z": fields["z"],
                    "stencil": fields["stencil"],
                    "mask": fields["color-mask"],
                })
    
    for frame in sorted(FRAMES):
        draws = sorted((row for row in rows if row["frame"] == frame), key=lambda row: row["cmd"])
        modes = collections.Counter(row["mode"] for row in draws)
        targets = collections.Counter(row["rt"] for row in draws)
        shader_pairs = {(row["vs"], row["ps"]) for row in draws}
        pipeline_states = {
            (row["vs"], row["ps"], row["blend"], row["alpha"], row["z"], row["stencil"], row["mask"], row["rt"], row["depth"])
            for row in draws
        }
        mode_transitions = []
        target_transitions = []
        state_transitions = 0
        for previous, current in zip(draws, draws[1:]):
            if previous["mode"] != current["mode"]:
                mode_transitions.append((previous["cmd"], previous["mode"], current["cmd"], current["mode"]))
            if previous["rt"] != current["rt"] or previous["depth"] != current["depth"]:
                target_transitions.append((previous["cmd"], previous["rt"], previous["depth"], current["cmd"], current["rt"], current["depth"]))
            previous_state = (previous["vs"], previous["ps"], previous["blend"], previous["alpha"], previous["z"], previous["stencil"], previous["mask"], previous["rt"], previous["depth"])
            current_state = (current["vs"], current["ps"], current["blend"], current["alpha"], current["z"], current["stencil"], current["mask"], current["rt"], current["depth"])
            if previous_state != current_state:
                state_transitions += 1
    
        # Count only returns from a blend/alpha draw to opaque later in the same attachment sequence.
        nonopaque_to_opaque_same_target = []
        for previous, current in zip(draws, draws[1:]):
            if previous["mode"] in {"blend", "alpha"} and current["mode"] == "opaque" and previous["rt"] == current["rt"] and previous["depth"] == current["depth"]:
                nonopaque_to_opaque_same_target.append((previous["cmd"], previous["mode"], current["cmd"], current["rt"], current["depth"]))
    
        print(f"frame={frame}")
        print(f"  draws={len(draws)} modes={dict(modes)} unique-shader-pairs={len(shader_pairs)} unique-pipeline-state-tuples={len(pipeline_states)}")
        print(f"  sequential-state-transitions={state_transitions} mode-transitions={len(mode_transitions)} target-depth-transitions={len(target_transitions)}")
        print(f"  nonopaque-to-opaque-same-target={len(nonopaque_to_opaque_same_target)}")
        print(f"  top-targets={targets.most_common(8)}")
        print(f"  mode-transition-detail={mode_transitions}")
        print(f"  nonopaque-return-detail={nonopaque_to_opaque_same_target}")

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import pathlib
    import re
    
    ROOT = pathlib.Path("/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp")
    SEARCH_ROOTS = [ROOT / "LibertyRecomp", ROOT / "LibertyRecompLib", ROOT / "glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src", ROOT / "glue/rexglue-sdk-main/gta4-recomp/src"]
    SKIP_PARTS = {"thirdparty", "generated", "out", "pseudocode"}
    
    pattern = re.compile(
        r"REXCVAR_DEFINE_(BOOL|INT32|UINT32|STRING)\s*\(\s*"
        r"([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s*,\s*([^,]+?)\s*,\s*\"([^\"]+)\"",
        re.DOTALL,
    )
    
    rows = []
    for search_root in SEARCH_ROOTS:
        if not search_root.exists():
            continue
        for path in search_root.rglob("*.cpp"):
            if any(part in SKIP_PARTS for part in path.parts):
                continue
            text = path.read_text(errors="replace")
            for match in pattern.finditer(text):
                flag_type, name, default, category = match.groups()
                diagnostic_name = any(token in name.lower() for token in ("trace", "diag", "profile", "debug", "log", "capture", "dump", "metrics", "oracle"))
                diagnostic_category = any(token in category.lower() for token in ("diag", "debug", "research", "log", "perf"))
                if not (diagnostic_name or diagnostic_category):
                    continue
                line = text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1
                rows.append((str(path), line, flag_type, name, " ".join(default.split()), category))
    
    for row in sorted(rows):
        print(f"{row[0]}:{row[1]} type={row[2]} name={row[3]} default={row[4]} category={row[5]}")

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import collections
    import pathlib
    import re
    
    ROOT = pathlib.Path("/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp")
    SEARCH_ROOTS = [ROOT / "LibertyRecomp", ROOT / "LibertyRecompLib", ROOT / "glue/rexglue-sdk-main/src", ROOT / "glue/rexglue-sdk-main/gta4-recomp/src"]
    SKIP_PARTS = {"thirdparty", "generated", "out", "pseudocode"}
    patterns = {
        "rexlog": re.compile(r"\bREX[A-Z0-9_]*LOG[A-Z0-9_]*\s*\("),
        "stdio": re.compile(r"\b(?:std::)?(?:f?printf|puts)\s*\("),
        "flush": re.compile(r"\b(?:std::)?fflush\s*\("),
        "iostream": re.compile(r"\bstd::(?:cerr|cout|clog)\b"),
        "diag_emit": re.compile(r"\bDIAG_EMIT\s*\("),
    }
    
    per_file = collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter)
    samples = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for search_root in SEARCH_ROOTS:
        if not search_root.exists():
            continue
        for path in search_root.rglob("*"):
            if not path.is_file() or path.suffix not in {".c", ".cc", ".cpp", ".h", ".hpp", ".mm"}:
                continue
            if any(part in SKIP_PARTS for part in path.parts):
                continue
            for line_number, line in enumerate(path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines(), 1):
                for category, pattern in patterns.items():
                    if pattern.search(line):
                        per_file[str(path)][category] += 1
                        if len(samples[category]) < 20:
                            samples[category].append((str(path), line_number, line.strip()))
    
    for path, counts in sorted(per_file.items(), key=lambda item: (-sum(item[1].values()), item[0])):
        total = sum(counts.values())
        print(f"{path} total={total} " + " ".join(f"{key}={counts[key]}" for key in patterns if counts[key]))
    
    print("\nTOTALS")
    totals = collections.Counter()
    for counts in per_file.values():
        totals.update(counts)
    for category in patterns:
        print(f"{category}={totals[category]}")

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import collections
    import glob
    import pathlib
    import re
    
    
    LOG_GLOB = (
        "/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/out/build/macos-release/"
        "LibertyRecomp/Liberty Recompiled.app/Contents/MacOS/logs/"
        "Liberty Recompiled_496*.log"
    )
    
    files = [pathlib.Path(path) for path in glob.glob(LOG_GLOB)]
    if not files:
        raise SystemExit("no run 496 logs found")
    
    patterns = {
        "native_trace": re.compile(r"\[NativeTrace\]"),
        "native_stage": re.compile(r"gta4-native-stage:"),
        "native_diag": re.compile(r"gta4-native-diag:"),
        "native_profiler": re.compile(r"NativeProfiler|gta4-native-profile"),
        "translucent_query": re.compile(r"point=translucent-query-result"),
        "translucent_split": re.compile(r"point=translucent-split"),
        "water_surface": re.compile(r"water-surface|water_e[0-9]|C64FD3C169FB7A5A"),
        "vehicle_glass": re.compile(r"vehicle-glass|vehglass", re.IGNORECASE),
        "light_sprite": re.compile(r"light-sprite|litsprite|FC2024B04FBB69BF", re.IGNORECASE),
        "depth_handoff": re.compile(r"point=explicit-depth-handoff(?:\s|$)"),
        "depth_probe": re.compile(r"point=depth-lifecycle-probe"),
        "guest_output_pixels": re.compile(r"\[GuestOutputPixels\]"),
        "watchdog": re.compile(r"Watchdog|XThread.*state|thread states", re.IGNORECASE),
        "resolve_origin": re.compile(r"\[ResolveOriginTrace\]"),
        "rendering_begin": re.compile(r"point=rendering-begin"),
        "content_probe": re.compile(r"point=(?:content|scene|depth|stencil)-.*probe"),
        "fault": re.compile(
            r"CRASH DETECTED|ACCESS_VIOLATION|EXC_BAD_ACCESS|Validation Error|"
            r"VUID-|device lost|DEVICE_LOST",
            re.IGNORECASE,
        ),
    }
    
    counts = collections.Counter()
    point_counts = collections.Counter()
    frame_occurrences = collections.Counter()
    present_frames: set[int] = set()
    trace_frames: set[int] = set()
    query_categories = collections.Counter()
    fault_examples: list[tuple[str, int, str]] = []
    first_timestamp = None
    last_timestamp = None
    total_lines = 0
    
    frame_re = re.compile(r"\bframe=(\d+)")
    present_re = re.compile(r"gta4-native-present: frame=(\d+)")
    trace_frame_re = re.compile(r"\[NativeTrace\] frame=(\d+)")
    point_re = re.compile(r"\bpoint=([^\s]+)")
    category_re = re.compile(r"\bcategory=([^\s]+)")
    timestamp_re = re.compile(r"^\[([^\]]+)\]")
    
    for path in files:
        with path.open("r", errors="replace") as stream:
            for line_number, line in enumerate(stream, 1):
                total_lines += 1
                timestamp_match = timestamp_re.match(line)
                if timestamp_match:
                    timestamp = timestamp_match.group(1)
                    if first_timestamp is None or timestamp < first_timestamp:
                        first_timestamp = timestamp
                    if last_timestamp is None or timestamp > last_timestamp:
                        last_timestamp = timestamp
    
                for name, pattern in patterns.items():
                    if pattern.search(line):
                        counts[name] += 1
    
                for match in frame_re.finditer(line):
                    frame_occurrences[int(match.group(1))] += 1
    
                present_match = present_re.search(line)
                if present_match:
                    present_frames.add(int(present_match.group(1)))
    
                trace_match = trace_frame_re.search(line)
                if trace_match:
                    trace_frames.add(int(trace_match.group(1)))
    
                if "[NativeTrace]" in line:
                    point_match = point_re.search(line)
                    if point_match:
                        point_counts[point_match.group(1)] += 1
    
                if "point=translucent-query-result" in line:
                    category_match = category_re.search(line)
                    query_categories[
                        category_match.group(1) if category_match else "<missing>"
                    ] += 1
    
                if patterns["fault"].search(line) and len(fault_examples) < 20:
                    fault_examples.append((path.name, line_number, line.rstrip()))
    
    print(f"files={len(files)}")
    print(f"total_lines={total_lines}")
    print(f"first_timestamp={first_timestamp}")
    print(f"last_timestamp={last_timestamp}")
    if frame_occurrences:
        print(f"all_frame_min={min(frame_occurrences)}")
        print(f"all_frame_max={max(frame_occurrences)}")
    print(f"present_unique={len(present_frames)}")
    if present_frames:
        print(f"present_min={min(present_frames)}")
        print(f"present_max={max(present_frames)}")
    print(f"trace_unique={len(trace_frames)}")
    print("trace_frames=" + ",".join(str(value) for value in sorted(trace_frames)))
    
    print("counts:")
    for name in sorted(patterns):
        print(f"  {name}={counts[name]}")
    
    print("top_native_trace_points:")
    for point, count in point_counts.most_common(25):
        print(f"  {point}={count}")
    
    print("translucent_query_categories:")
    for category, count in query_categories.most_common():
        print(f"  {category}={count}")
    
    print("fault_examples:")
    for path_name, line_number, line in fault_examples:
        print(f"  {path_name}:{line_number}:{line}")

    +        for line in stream:
    +            combined_lines += 1
    +            for name, pattern in combined_patterns.items():
    +                if pattern.search(line):
    +                    combined_counts[name] += 1
    +    print("combined_capture:")
    +    print(f"  bytes={combined_path.stat().st_size}")
    +    print(f"  lines={combined_lines}")
    +    for name in sorted(combined_patterns):
    +        print(f"  {name}={combined_counts[name]}")
    +
    +print("persistent_capture:")

## Phase 1 — Diagnostics launch gate

This must land first because normal launches currently perform logging, GPU queries, replay draws, readbacks, and watchdog work.

Launch contract:

- Normal launch: diagnostics mask is zero.
- `--diagnostics`: enable all diagnostics.
- `--diagnostics-categories=native-trace,native-profiler,presenter,...`: enable selected categories.
- Unknown categories or categories without `--diagnostics` are CLI errors.
- The master flag is command-line-only: not a CVar, environment variable, TOML setting, or saved preference.

Implementation design:

- Parse it before the current logger initialization in [main.cpp](/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/LibertyRecomp/main.cpp:488).
- Store one immutable process-wide category mask in `rexruntime`.
- Pass the mask explicitly across the GPU-plugin ABI through `GpuCreateInfo`.
- Gate work before counters, formatting, hashing, allocation, query creation, render-scope breaks, replay draws, readbacks, waits, file creation, or `fflush`.
- Normal launches create no log sink, log directory, rotating file, stdout/unified-log output, watchdog thread, presenter capture, Vulkan debug messenger, or diagnostic GPU commands.
- Preserve a separate lazy emergency path for actual crashes, device loss, allocation failures, and fatal errors.
- Existing diagnostic CVars become subordinate and cannot activate anything without the master flag.
- Fix CVar precedence separately so runtime/CLI values properly outrank environment/config values.

This covers the native renderer, presenter, guest hooks, physics, legal-screen tracing, CoreAudio analysis, Vulkan debugging, watchdog, transition recorder, and raw `fprintf`/`fflush` sites.

Acceptance requires a normal bounded launch to produce:

- No new log file or log directory.
- No diagnostic stdout/stderr.
- No `/tmp` image captures.
- No watchdog or transition thread.
- No diagnostic queries, copies, readbacks, replay draws, or render-pass breaks.
- Identical rendered output to a diagnostics-compiled-out build.

CLI11 supports a two-stage parse with remaining arguments, matching this design. [CLI11 documentation](https://github.com/CLIUtils/CLI11)

## Phase 2 — Clean measurement foundation

Four separate modes:

| Mode | Trace | Profiler | Purpose |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| B0 | Off | Off | Real external baseline |
| B1 | On | Off | Quantify diagnostic overhead |
| B2 | Off | Phase ranges | Broad GPU attribution |
| B3 | Off | One-frame command detail | Inspect one identified hotspot |

Run 496 proved why this separation is required:

- 41 traced frames.
- 34,518 `NativeTrace` records.
- Periodic diagnostic frames reached 982–989 ms around the handoff cadence.
- Queries, content probes, render-scope breaks, and three replay variants were active.

The existing profiler must not run alongside native tracing because its sampled frame waits for the preceding heavyweight trace submission.

Every benchmark will use fixed save, camera, weather, time, resolution, reflection settings, shader overrides, present mode, and semantic command fingerprint. Analysis remains Python-only.

## Phase 3 — GPU measurement and fixes

Priority order:

1. Combined depth/stencil resolve.
2. Depth handoff:
   - stencil save;
   - resolved-depth copy;
   - stencil restore.
3. Reflection rendering, resolves, and tail mips by family.
4. Title composite/post-FX.
5. Deferred light-volume stencil/shading pairs.
6. Water, glass, vehicle lights, sprites, and emissive families.

### Depth handoff

The handoff ran in all 571 consecutive gameplay frames examined. Its current path performs a combined resolve plus six barriers and three fullscreen transfers. The nominal logical data processed is 78.600586 MiB per frame, but Apple GPU counters must determine real device-memory traffic.

Candidate sequence:

1. Correct and narrow depth/stencil barriers one site at a time. Current resolve code uses color-attachment access masks for a depth/stencil resolve; Khronos documents depth/stencil attachment stages and access masks separately. [Vulkan synchronization examples](https://docs.vulkan.org/guide/latest/synchronization_examples.html)
2. Measure stencil save, depth copy, and restore independently.
3. Only if transfers dominate, test a depth-only destination operation that loads/preserves the existing stencil.
4. Consider binding the explicit title-resolved depth resource directly to the forward path only after lifetime and write semantics are proven.

We will not source from the cleared AA attachment, restore placement scanning, introduce EDRAM aliasing, or change alpha semantics.

### Reflections

Measure mirror, water, and environment reflection rendering separately, including base resolve and every tail mip.

Possible fixes depend on counters:

- Native resolve where format/sample compatibility permits.
- Linear blits instead of fullscreen tail-mip passes where output equivalence passes.
- Resolution/update-frequency policies only if reflection rendering itself dominates; those are explicit quality tradeoffs.

### Post-FX correction

Fresh run 496 proves the custom split and sun-shaft passes are currently dormant:

- All 16 attempts selected `D9132320`, format 130/D32S8, as the supposed color input.
- The color-aspect check rejected it before snapshot or pass recording.

Therefore those passes are not causing the current GPU regression. Their source wiring is a separate correctness task. Once activation is fixed and proven, we can measure their four-pass chains and copybacks before considering chaining or fusion.

### Translucency and deferred lights

No unsafe global sorting or draw removal.

Potential changes only after counters:

- Adjacent batching when pipeline, resources, constants, and ordering semantics are identical.
- Per-light/per-draw screen bounds or scissors if fragment overdraw dominates.
- Descriptor/state reuse if CPU recording dominates.
- Preserve stencil-volume → additive-light dependencies and blend ordering.

Apple’s TBDR guidance makes attachment traffic, load/store actions, and blended overdraw important measurement targets. [Apple TBDR guidance](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/tailor-your-apps-for-apple-gpus-and-tile-based-deferred-rendering), [GPU bandwidth counters](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/measuring-the-gpus-use-of-memory-bandwidth)

## Phase 4 — CPU and pacing fixes

Measured candidates:

1. Per-draw descriptor allocation and updates.
2. Repeated constant uploads.
3. Texture creation/upload bursts.
4. Linear pipeline lookup and synchronous pipeline misses.
5. MoltenVK submission encoding.
6. One native frame in flight.
7. Actual WSI acquire/present latency.

Planned decision tree:

- Descriptor reuse only if exact binding reuse and update cost are material. Khronos explicitly recommends avoiding per-frame allocation/update when reuse is possible. [Descriptor-management guidance](https://docs.vulkan.org/samples/latest/samples/performance/descriptor_management/README.html)
- Same-frame constant-block reuse only after hash plus byte-equality validation.
- Texture suballocation/batching/asynchronous uploads only after separating allocation, conversion, copy encoding, and readiness costs.
- Hash-map pipeline lookup or loading-phase precreation only after lookup/miss timing proves value. [Pipeline-cache guidance](https://docs.vulkan.org/samples/latest/samples/performance/pipeline_cache/README.html)
- Test MoltenVK synchronous submission and prefill modes as an A/B matrix. MoltenVK currently defaults to caller-thread submission and submit-time Metal encoding. [MoltenVK configuration](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/MoltenVK/blob/main/Docs/MoltenVK_Configuration_Parameters.md)
- Multiple frames in flight comes last. First refactor to a one-context `FrameContext`, then make resource retirement submission-aware, then compare one/two/three contexts. Apple commonly recommends keeping CPU work ahead of the GPU, but resource lifetime correctness must come first. [Apple command-buffer guidance](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/3DDrawing/Conceptual/MTLBestPracticesGuide/CommandBuffers.html)

## Promotion gate for every optimization

Every patch gets its own rollback boundary and must pass simultaneously:

- Opaque/deferred scene changes the target.
- Water renders and changes the target.
- Vehicle and general glass render.
- Vehicle lights render.
- Representative light sprite renders.
- Forward depth is current, nonuniform, and not cleared zero/stale one.
- Destination stencil checksum is unchanged where required.
- Final composite and presentation are finite and nonblack.
- No target/resolve failure, validation error, or device loss.
- Repeated scripted timing shows a statistically repeatable improvement without moving equivalent cost elsewhere.

The first implementation should be the diagnostics launch gate. Only after its no-flag acceptance passes should we collect the clean baseline that decides which renderer optimization comes next.

The instrumented run is still booting (export appears after ~960 rendered frames). While it finishes, here is the complete manual review. I'll follow up with the measured per-range numbers as soon as the capture lands.

Native renderer performance review — findings

What this change set actually is

The committed baseline (873b68a8) contains the translucency feature and a large amount of always-on diagnostics. The ~3,000-line uncommitted diff in graphics_system.cpp is mostly mitigation-in-flight: gating diagnostics behind the command-line rex::diagnostics policy (default off), a rewritten sampling profiler, and an experimental "attachment" depth-handoff transport. That context matters because the regression has two separable components — feature cost and diagnostic cost — and which one you see depends on how the app is launched.

Root causes of the average GPU-time increase (≈4 ms → ≈10 ms)

1. The deferred→forward transition added with translucency is heavyweight. Once per frame, gta4_native_hooks.cpp:3552 submits five full-screen resolve/convert passes (depth + 4 color targets) plus a depth-surface handoff. The handoff's default "buffer" transport (graphics_system.cpp:9989) performs three full-screen transfer copies per frame — stencil→scratch buffer, depth image→image, scratch buffer→stencil — with 4–5 pipeline barriers between them. I computed the raw bandwidth in Python: only ~11 MB/frame (~1.3 GB/s at 120 FPS), which is trivial — so the cost is not bandwidth. It's the structure: each copy/resolve forces a render-pass break, and on Apple's TBDR GPU every break means flushing tile memory to system memory and reloading it, which Apple's own guidance identifies as the dominant per-pass cost (Metal Best Practices: Load and Store Actions, WWDC20: Harness Apple GPUs with Metal). This runs through MoltenVK (confirmed: the app bundles libMoltenVK.dylib), where each pass break is also a Metal encoder switch (MoltenVK transfer command implementation).

2. Serializing barriers. The baseline code guarded these copies with VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_ALL_COMMANDS_BIT source stages, which drains the whole GPU pipeline at each barrier instead of overlapping work across it — Khronos and the Vulkan samples explicitly call this out as a throughput killer (Vulkan-Samples: pipeline barriers, Khronos: Understanding Vulkan Synchronization). The uncommitted diff already narrows these to precise scopes via GetDepthImageAccessScope (depth_handoff_util.h) — that's the right direction and should be kept.

3. The translucent forward draws themselves (water/glass/sprites, blending overdraw) are real feature cost but are unlikely to be 6 ms on their own at this resolution — the pass-break structure above is the prime suspect. The new profiler's GPU ranges (kStencilSave, kDepthCopy, kStencilRestore, kTranslucent*, kOpaqueControl…) are precisely the instrument to split this; see measurement section.

Root causes of the choppiness / frame-to-frame variance

1. Diagnostic frames fire periodically in the regressed build. gta4_trace_native_renderer defaults to true (graphics_system.cpp:87). At the committed baseline (no policy gates), every 120th frame becomes a "diagnostic frame" that: initializes a 1024-slot occlusion query pool, wraps every translucent draw in a begin/end occlusion query, re-draws each categorized translucent draw up to four times (original + depth-only + stencil-only + raster-only "deep capture", graphics_system.cpp:15324), records content probes (image copies + host readback + render-pass breaks), and logs hundreds of REXLOG lines. One expensive frame every ~1–1.5 s is exactly the periodic hitching described. In the working tree this is gated behind --diagnostics — but note --diagnostics with no category list enables all categories, so a habit of launching with plain --diagnostics reproduces the choppiness on the new build too.

2. Per-frame CPU overhead at the committed baseline (now fixed in the diff, worth keeping):
- Every TraceNativeRendererEvent call site evaluated its fmt::format(...) argument before the trace-enabled check — thousands of string formats + allocations per frame (~1,200 commands/frame per the session logs). The diff's macro at graphics_system.cpp:1520 fixes argument evaluation.
- RecordIndexedPrimitive scanned every index of every indexed draw on CPU for min/max diagnostics each frame; now gated.
- Per-frame counter/bookkeeping churn now behind collect_frame_diagnostics.

3. The frame architecture makes every spike visible. The render callback waits for the previous submission's fence before recording the next frame (graphics_system.cpp:15968) — single frame in flight, so frame time ≈ GPU time + CPU record time with zero overlap. My Python model reproduces the reported numbers almost exactly: 4 ms GPU + 4 ms CPU = 125 FPS; 10 ms GPU + 2–4 ms CPU = 71–83 FPS. Standard guidance is 2+ frames in flight so CPU recording overlaps GPU execution (Vulkan docs: Frames in flight, vkguide: Double buffering). This predates translucency, but it's why the +6 ms GPU regression converted 1:1 into FPS loss and why any variance shows as chop.

4. First-use pipeline creation hitches. Translucent materials introduce new blend-state/shader pipeline permutations created at draw time via vkCreateGraphicsPipelines. There is a disk-persisted VkPipelineCache, which mitigates repeat runs, but new permutations still trigger MoltenVK's SPIR-V→MSL conversion + Metal PSO compile mid-frame — a well-documented hitch source (Khronos: Reducing draw-time hitching, Vulkan-Samples: pipeline cache, MoltenVK discussion #1789). Expect this specifically when glass/water first appears — matching "choppiness appeared with translucent rendering."

5. ReleaseUnusedTextureImages() runs every frame (graphics_system.cpp:6760): rebuilds a hash set over all texture resources and destroys any image whose guest resource vanished — with no aging. A texture that is released and re-registered across frames (watertex generation targets are candidates) causes vkCreateImage+vkAllocateMemory+re-upload churn. Worth confirming with the kUploadBytes counter — steady non-zero upload on static scenes would indicate thrash.

Deterministic measurement (no code changes needed)

The rewritten profiler is exactly the microbenchmark harness needed, and it exports machine-readable per-range samples:

REX_GTA4_PROFILE_NATIVE_INTERVAL=8 REX_GTA4_PROFILE_NATIVE_SAMPLES=120 "./out/build/macos-release/LibertyRecomp/Liberty Recompiled.app/Contents/MacOS/Liberty Recompiled" --skip-logos --diagnostics --diagnostics-categories native-profiler

This samples 1 frame in 8 and writes ~/Library/Application Support/LibertyRecomp/Diagnostics/native-performance-latest.log with per-frame GPU ticks for each range (frame, depth-copy, stencil-save/restore, each translucent family, reflections, composite, present) plus CPU ranges (fence-wait, record, submit) and counters. Enabling only native-profiler keeps trace/probe/translucency-query overhead out of the measurement. I have this exact run going right now and will report the numbers when the export lands. Key A/B levers, all config-only:

┌────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ Handoff transport  │ gta4_depth_handoff_transport buffer vs attachment       │ 3-copy transport vs single fullscreen depth/stencil-write draw │
├────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Diagnostic frames  │ --diagnostics-categories with/without native-trace etc. │ periodic-hitch component                                       │
├────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Choppiness profile │ kFenceWait vs kFrame CPU/GPU ranges across 120 samples  │ GPU-bound vs record-bound frames, variance                     │
└────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Recommendations (not implemented, per your instruction)

1. Land the diagnostics gating diff — it removes the fmt-evaluation, index-scan, and periodic diagnostic-frame costs from production.
2. Measure the "attachment" handoff transport — replacing 3 transfer copies + barriers with one fullscreen draw writing depth (stencil preserved by LOAD_OP_LOAD) avoids two pass breaks; this is the TBDR-friendly shape per Apple's load/store guidance. It's already implemented behind the cvar; it needs validation + measurement, not new code.
3. Longer term: 2 frames in flight (per-frame command buffers + fences) so CPU record overlaps GPU — this alone should recover most of the FPS delta even at 10 ms GPU, and it halves the visibility of any one-frame spike.
4. Consider batching the five transition resolves into fewer passes / subresource copies, and age-based texture eviction instead of same-frame eviction.
5. When running with diagnostics for debugging, pass an explicit category list — plain --diagnostics enables everything, including the 4×-redraw translucent deep captures.

void Gta4NativeGraphicsSystem::ActivateNativeFrameSlot(NativeFrameSlot& slot) {
  command_pool_ = slot.command_pool;
  command_buffer_ = slot.command_buffer;
  upload_buffer_ = slot.upload_buffer;
  descriptor_sets_[5] = slot.upload_descriptor_set;
  frame_descriptor_pool_ = slot.frame_descriptor_pool;
  frame_descriptor_draw_capacity_ = slot.frame_descriptor_draw_capacity;
  frame_descriptor_resolve_capacity_ = slot.frame_descriptor_resolve_capacity;
  frame_descriptor_combined_set_capacity_ =
      slot.frame_descriptor_combined_set_capacity;
}

void Gta4NativeGraphicsSystem::StoreNativeFrameSlot(NativeFrameSlot& slot) {
  slot.command_pool = command_pool_;
  slot.command_buffer = command_buffer_;
  slot.upload_buffer = upload_buffer_;
  slot.upload_descriptor_set = descriptor_sets_[5];
  slot.frame_descriptor_pool = frame_descriptor_pool_;
  slot.frame_descriptor_draw_capacity = frame_descriptor_draw_capacity_;
  slot.frame_descriptor_resolve_capacity = frame_descriptor_resolve_capacity_;
  slot.frame_descriptor_combined_set_capacity =
      frame_descriptor_combined_set_capacity_;
}

Build resumed (same log, the existing monitor still watches it — it reports errors, the link line, and BUILD_EXIT automatically).

Grabbing an execution log — the short version

One-liner (bounded run, log preserved) — this is all you have to do:

.claude/skills/libertyrecomp-build-run/scripts/macos_run_log.sh macos-release 30 /tmp/liberty_run.log

That runs the binary for 30 s and leaves the combined log at /tmp/liberty_run.log (exit 124 just means the time limit, not a crash).

Manual, when you want to play and reproduce something:

"./out/build/macos-release/LibertyRecomp/Liberty Recompiled.app/Contents/MacOS/Liberty Recompiled" --diagnostics --diagnostics-categories logging,native-trace 2>&1 | tee /tmp/liberty-exec.log

Reproduce the issue, quit normally, read /tmp/liberty-exec.log. Rotated per-run logs also land in out/build/macos-release/LibertyRecomp/Liberty Recompiled.app/Contents/MacOS/logs/.

Three things that matter:

1. No --diagnostics → no renderer logging at all. That's by design now; a plain launch is the fast production path.
2. Pick categories deliberately — logging alone gives general app logs; add native-trace/native-probes/native-translucency only when debugging the renderer, since any of those (by design) also drops the renderer back to serialized single-frame submissions and re-enables the periodic heavy diagnostic frames. --diagnostics with no category list turns everything on — that's the choppiness-reproducing mode, avoid it for perf testing.
3. Perf numbers come from the profiler category instead: --diagnostics --diagnostics-categories native-profiler,logging, then read ~/Library/Application Support/LibertyRecomp/Diagnostics/native-performance-latest.log after ~31 sampled frames (interval tunable via REX_GTA4_PROFILE_NATIVE_INTERVAL, sample count via REX_GTA4_PROFILE_NATIVE_SAMPLES).

One correction to the codex snippet you pasted: I don't see a --gpu_plugin flag defined in main.cpp (the CLI only defines install/video/diagnostics flags and tolerates extras, so the flag is silently ignored) — the native renderer is selected by config, not that switch. MTL_HUD_ENABLED=1 is fine and orthogonal (Metal's FPS overlay).

When the build finishes I'll rebuild unit_tests against this tree, rerun the suite, and report final status.

What shipped (all in glue/rexglue-sdk-main, none in the deadweight folder)

1. Two frames in flight — CPU record now overlaps GPU execution. Per-slot command pool/buffer, upload buffer + its storage descriptor set, and frame descriptor pool; frame N waits only its own slot's fence (N−2) instead of frame N−1. Since frame time was previously GPU + CPU serialized, this alone should recover a large share of the 120→70-90 FPS drop.
2. Automatic safety fallback — enabling any capture category (native-trace, native-probes, native-translucency, native-profiler) or setting gta4_native_frames_in_flight=1 restores the exact old serialized behavior, so diagnostics readbacks stay correct and there's an instant rollback knob.
3. Age-based texture eviction — images survive a 240-frame grace window instead of being destroyed on the first unreferenced frame (kills create/upload churn and is required for in-flight safety). A compile-time assert also ties the presenter mailbox depth to the frames-in-flight count.
4. Tests — native_frame_scheduling_test.cpp locks in the serialization matrix, slot rotation, wait-fence selection, and the eviction-grace ≥ frames-in-flight safety bound.
