Good instinct to check, but it's not frozen — the two follow-up snapshots (5 s apart) show completely different stacks each time and the process is running at 240% CPU:

- Snapshot 1: main thread waiting in MoltenVK nextDrawable (momentary swapchain-drawable wait — normal when all 3 drawables are briefly outstanding, or the window is occluded).
- Snapshots 2–3: main thread actively encoding Metal work — AGXMetalG13X endEncoding, MVKCommandEncodingContext::syncFences, allocating new MTLCommandBuffers. The render worker's mutex wait from the first snapshot is gone too.

So every "blocked" frame I caught first was transient; the threads are churning through work. What you're seeing is the boot/world-init phase — from earlier sessions this game sits in sub_821200D0 world init for 60+ seconds with a mostly static screen while streaming, audio RPF loading, and the one-time particle-emitter registration storm run, which reads as "frozen" while CPU burns.

Two incidental observations worth keeping:

1. MoltenVK is encoding command buffers on the submitting thread (MVKQueue::submit → encode inline), meaning our vkQueueSubmit cost includes full Metal encoding — that's MoltenVK's synchronous-submit mode, and it's part of why CPU record/submit time matters so much here.
2. The freeze-vs-alive test is trivial to repeat yourself:

lldb --batch -p $(pgrep -f "Liberty Recompiled" | head -1) -o "bt 5" -o "detach" -o "quit"

Run it twice ~5 s apart: identical top frames + ~0% CPU in ps = real hang (grab bt all and send it to me); changing frames + high CPU = it's working. Give it a minute or two — if the HUD appears and frames start flowing, we're in the new overlapped path and I'd love to know what the frame-time graph looks like.

Real data at last — and the story is now complete. One more 2-minute A/B (MSAA off) to quantify the biggest GPU lever, then the full report:

Yes — profiled, with the renderer's own GPU timestamp profiler, three captures deep. Here's what the data says while the MSAA A/B finishes:

Profiling results (100 sampled frames, 1→2476, attract-mode world content)

GPU per frame — mean 6.2 ms, median 3.7 ms, p95 21.8 ms, max 29 ms. The scene ranges break down as: present 2.2 ms, environment-reflections 1.7 ms, composite 1.4 ms, depth-resolve 0.9 ms, water-reflections 0.7 ms, depth-copy+stencil-save/restore (the handoff) 0.8 ms, translucent families ~0.8 ms combined. So no single scene pass is huge — the frame cost is spread wide, and the median-vs-p95 spread (3.7 → 21.8 ms) says the GPU load itself fluctuates ~6× between light and heavy frames. That's your FPS variance on the GPU side, and it's all being paid at 3456×2168 with 2×MSAA.

CPU per frame — this is the chug. render-callback median is only 9.7 ms, but p95 = 150 ms and max = 1.59 seconds:

┌─────────────────────┬─────┬───────┬────────┐
│      CPU range      │ p50 │  p95  │  max   │
├─────────────────────┼─────┼───────┼────────┤
│ render-callback     │ 9.7 │ 150.4 │ 1590.6 │
├─────────────────────┼─────┼───────┼────────┤
│ command-recording   │ 0.1 │ 27.5  │ 1182.5 │
├─────────────────────┼─────┼───────┼────────┤
│ queue-submit        │ 5.8 │ 38.1  │ 993.9  │
├─────────────────────┼─────┼───────┼────────┤
│ fence-wait          │ 3.1 │ 20.3  │ 907.7  │
├─────────────────────┼─────┼───────┼────────┤
│ texture-preparation │ 0.1 │ 12.1  │ 360.3  │
└─────────────────────┴─────┴───────┴────────┘

Most frames are fine; periodically one frame eats hundreds of milliseconds to 1.6 s of CPU. Those spikes line up with command-recording/queue-submit (first-use vkCreateGraphicsPipelines → MoltenVK SPIR-V→MSL → Metal PSO compile, exactly the draw-time hitching Khronos documents) and texture-preparation + upload-bytes spikes up to 23.6 MB in a single frame (streaming uploads through the frame upload buffer, encoded inline during vkQueueSubmit). That is the chugging — not the translucency feature's steady GPU cost, and not the frames-in-flight change (which measurably doubled throughput, 6240 vs 3120 frames in identical 90 s runs).

So the fix list, in impact order, is: (1) pipeline pre-warm/async compile so PSO builds never happen mid-frame, (2) amortize/async the streaming texture uploads instead of single-frame 23 MB bursts, (3) resolution/MSAA cost — which the running A/B capture is about to quantify. I'll report that comparison as soon as it exports.

Profiling complete — three controlled captures plus two A/Bs, all with the renderer's own GPU-timestamp profiler. Here's the full picture:

Where the performance actually goes

1. The chug is CPU hitches, not steady GPU load. In the MSAA-on capture, the render callback's median is a healthy 9.7 ms but p95 is 150 ms and the worst frame took 1.59 seconds. The spikes decompose into first-use pipeline creation (command-recording max 1.18 s — Metal PSO compilation at draw time through MoltenVK) and streaming texture uploads (up to 23.6 MB in one frame, encoded inline during vkQueueSubmit). Every one of those spikes is a visible stutter.

2. MSAA 2× at retina resolution is the single biggest steady cost. A/B with identical profiling setups:

┌──────────────────────────┬─────────┬──────────┬─────────────────────┐
│          metric          │ msaa 2x │ msaa off │        delta        │
├──────────────────────────┼─────────┼──────────┼─────────────────────┤
│ frames rendered in 110 s │ 2400    │ 4200     │ 1.75× faster        │
├──────────────────────────┼─────────┼──────────┼─────────────────────┤
│ GPU frame p95            │ 21.8 ms │ 4.8 ms   │ 4.6× (caveat below) │
├──────────────────────────┼─────────┼──────────┼─────────────────────┤
│ present pass mean        │ 2.19 ms │ 1.35 ms  │ 1.6×                │
└──────────────────────────┴─────────┴──────────┴─────────────────────┘

(Caveat: the MSAA-off run reached each frame number earlier in wall time, so its sample window caught less world content — the honest headline is the 1.75× wall-clock throughput, not the 4.6×.) The default is gta4_native_msaa = "2x" on top of 3456×2168 surfaces — about 16× the Xbox 360's pixel-sample load.

3. The frames-in-flight fix works as designed — identical 90 s runs: 6240 frames overlapped vs 3120 serialized, exactly 2.0×. The remaining low FPS is items 1–2, not submission pacing.

4. The translucency feature itself is cheap — depth-copy + stencil save/restore total ~0.8 ms, all translucent families ~0.8 ms. The original suspicion about the feature's draw cost is dead; it was the diagnostics (now gated) plus everything above.

What I'd implement next, in impact order

1. Async/pre-warmed pipeline creation — kill the 0.3–1.2 s PSO hitches (biggest chug win).
2. Amortized texture streaming — cap per-frame upload bytes, spread big streams over frames (second chug win).
3. Expose/lower the AA default — gta4_native_msaa=off (or a render-scale option) is an immediate 1.75× for users who prefer frame rate (config-only, zero code).

Want me to implement 1 and 2? For an instant improvement today, set gta4_native_msaa = "off" in config.toml — that's measured, not speculative.

void Gta4NativeGraphicsSystem::PipelineCompilerThreadMain() {
  rex::thread::SetCurrentThreadName("GTA4 Pipeline Compiler");
  for (;;) {
    NativePipelineCompileJob job;
    {
      std::unique_lock lock(pipeline_compiler_mutex_);
      pipeline_compiler_condition_.wait(lock, [this]() {
        return pipeline_compiler_stop_ || !pipeline_compile_queue_.empty();
      });
      if (pipeline_compiler_stop_ && pipeline_compile_queue_.empty()) {
        return;
      }
      job = std::move(pipeline_compile_queue_.front());
      pipeline_compile_queue_.pop_front();
    }
    // The default-flag pipeline cache is internally synchronized for
    // vkCreateGraphicsPipelines, so compiling here is safe; the cache is only
    // serialized to disk after this thread has been joined.
    const VkPipeline pipeline = CreateNativePipelineFromJob(job);
    {
      std::lock_guard lock(pipeline_compiler_mutex_);
      // Failures are published as null handles so the render thread caches
      // the rejection instead of re-enqueueing the same job every frame.
      completed_pipelines_.push_back({job.key, pipeline});
    }
  }
}

void Gta4NativeGraphicsSystem::DrainCompletedNativePipelines() {
  std::vector<NativePipeline> completed;
  {
    std::lock_guard lock(pipeline_compiler_mutex_);
    completed.swap(completed_pipelines_);
  }
  for (NativePipeline& native_pipeline : completed) {
    pending_pipeline_keys_.erase(
        std::remove(pending_pipeline_keys_.begin(),
                    pending_pipeline_keys_.end(), native_pipeline.key),
        pending_pipeline_keys_.end());
    if (native_pipeline.pipeline) {
      native_pipeline_cache_dirty_ = true;
    }
    native_pipelines_.push_back(native_pipeline);
  }
}

void Gta4NativeGraphicsSystem::StopNativePipelineCompiler() {
  {
    std::lock_guard lock(pipeline_compiler_mutex_);
    pipeline_compiler_stop_ = true;
    pipeline_compile_queue_.clear();
  }
  pipeline_compiler_condition_.notify_all();
  if (pipeline_compiler_thread_.joinable()) {
    pipeline_compiler_thread_.join();
  }
  pipeline_compiler_thread_ = std::thread();
  // Adopt any pipelines the worker finished so shutdown destroys them.
  DrainCompletedNativePipelines();
  pending_pipeline_keys_.clear();
}

Implemented in this pass

1. Async pipeline compilation (graphics_system.cpp)
- GetOrCreatePipeline split: the render thread builds the key, settles alpha-test specialization, and dispatches; a dedicated "GTA4 Pipeline Compiler" thread runs vkCreateGraphicsPipelines. - Verified against documentation before writing: a default-flag VkPipelineCache is internally synchronized for concurrent pipeline creation (Vulkan refpage), MoltenVK supports background pipeline compilation (MoltenVK docs), and skip-until-ready is the accepted mitigation for draw-time hitching (Khronos). The compiler thread is joined before vkGetPipelineCacheData at shutdown (that call does require external sync). Failures are cached as null so bad states never re-hitch. Rollback: gta4_native_async_pipelines = false.

2. Per-frame texture upload budget (native_streaming_budget.h)
- Streaming uploads capped at 8 MiB/frame (gta4_native_upload_budget_kib, 0 = off); over-budget textures upload on following frames and sample the existing null-texture descriptor fallback meanwhile. The present source is offered first so it can never be deferred, and the first payload is always admitted so progress is guaranteed. This flattens the 23 MB single-frame upload bursts the profiler caught.

❯ why tf and i seeing faint images ontop opf the actaul games frames?? in your most recent build its 130fps now but i see compelte black 'Yeah — that is frame ghosting / stale-frame persistence. You’re seeing remnants of earlier frames composited over the current one.
  From your screenshots, the giveaway is that the faint image is not motion blur tied to an object. It’s a whole previous camera view lingering at low opacity. In the second and third shots you can see geometry/text from a prior frame surviving underneath the new scene.
  Given the timing, the most likely cause is one of the renderer changes around multiple frames in flight / async work, not the PSO compiler by itself.
  What probably happened is one of these:

  * A render target or swapchain image is being reused before the previous frame has fully finished.
  * A frame-local texture/depth/color resource was changed from effectively single-buffered to multi-frame use without becoming per-frame indexed.
  * The render pass is using `LOAD` / preserving attachment contents where it previously relied on serialized execution, so stale pixels survive.
  * The new async texture/pipeline path is exposing a synchronization bug that was hidden when `frames_in_flight = 1`.
  * A composite/history/intermediate target is being read from the wrong frame slot.
  * Less likely: the final framebuffer is not fully overwritten every frame, so old pixels remain wherever the new frame has transparency/blending.

  The strongest clue is the prior test:
  FIF=2 doubled throughput versus FIF=1.
  That means the optimization changed the execution model from serialized rendering to overlapped rendering. Any resource that was implicitly safe only because frame N finished before frame N+1 began can now produce exactly this.
  The fastest diagnostic is not to rewrite anything. Run the same scene with:

  ```toml
  gta4_native_frames_in_flight = 1
  ```

  If the ghosting disappears completely, you have basically proven that the bug is a frames-in-flight resource-lifetime/synchronization issue.
  Then the code review should focus specifically on every resource surviving across `Render()` calls:

  ```text
  swapchain image
  final composite target
  resolved color
  resolved depth
  deferred color targets
  reflection textures
  translucency intermediates
  upload buffers
  descriptor-backed temporary textures
  command pools / command buffers
  fences / semaphores
  ```

  Every mutable resource has to fall into one of two categories:

  ```text
  A. genuinely shared
     → explicit synchronization before reuse

  B. frame-local
     → resource[frameIndex]
  ```

  For example, this becomes unsafe with two frames in flight:

  ```cpp
  Texture compositeTexture;
  ```

  if frame N+1 starts writing it before frame N has finished reading it.
  It may need to conceptually become:

  ```cpp
  Texture compositeTexture[kFramesInFlight];
  ```

  and use:

  ```cpp
  compositeTexture[currentFrameIndex]
  ```

  The other thing I would inspect immediately is the final render-pass attachment configuration. If it looks like:

  ```cpp
  loadOp = VK_ATTACHMENT_LOAD_OP_LOAD;
  ```

  for a target expected to start clean each frame, you’re deliberately preserving the previous contents.
  For a completely redrawn attachment you’d normally expect either:

  ```cpp
  VK_ATTACHMENT_LOAD_OP_CLEAR
  ```

  or:

  ```cpp
  VK_ATTACHMENT_LOAD_OP_DONT_CARE
  ```

  depending on whether you need a defined initial value.
  The visual appearance you’ve shown is especially consistent with a target being blended over stale contents. It looks almost like:

  ```text
  current frame × alpha
  +
  previous framebuffer × (1-alpha)
  ```

  rather than ordinary corruption.
  And there is one renderer subsystem I’d put under the microscope before everything else: the final composite/present path. Your earlier profiler already identified a `composite` pass and a separate `present` cost. If an intermediate composite surface became shared across the two active frame contexts, frame N and N+1 can contaminate each other even though the swapchain itself is synchronized correctly.
  So no, this isn’t your eyes and it isn’t normal GTA IV post-processing. Those screenshots show a renderer bug.

  FIF=1 → ghosting?
  FIF=2 → ghosting?

The biggest problem is the new async-pipeline implementation.

Your renderer now literally does this when it encounters a pipeline that has not finished compiling:

if (REXCVAR_GET(gta4_native_async_pipelines)) {
  if (std::find(pending_pipeline_keys_.begin(),
                pending_pipeline_keys_.end(),
                key) != pending_pipeline_keys_.end()) {
    // Still compiling; the draw is skipped until the pipeline is ready.
    return VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  }
  pending_pipeline_keys_.push_back(key);
  EnqueueNativePipelineJob(std::move(job));
  return VK_NULL_HANDLE;
}

And every normal draw path then does:

VkPipeline pipeline = GetOrCreatePipeline(...);
if (!pipeline) {
  return fail("pipeline");
}

So on the first frame containing a new PSO, that draw simply does not happen.

That is not equivalent to UnleashedRecomp’s renderer.

What UnleashedRecomp does differently

UnleashedRecomp has asynchronous pipeline compilation, but its architecture is built around precompilation, not “skip arbitrary game draws when a PSO is missing.”

It explicitly has:

Video::StartPipelinePrecompilation()

and later:

if (g_shouldPrecompilePipelines)
{
    EnqueuePipelineTask(
        PipelineTaskType::PrecompilePipelines, {});
}

It walks game/material/model information ahead of use and queues expected PipelineStates into several worker threads.

Then its normal render-thread fallback is:

static RenderPipeline*
CreateGraphicsPipelineInRenderThread(
    PipelineState pipelineState)
{
    ...
    if (pipeline == nullptr)
    {
        pipeline =
            CreateGraphicsPipeline(pipelineState);
    }
    return pipeline.get();
}

In other words:

UnleashedRecomp does not deliberately omit the draw merely because compilation is underway.

It may take a hitch if precompilation missed something, but the scene remains semantically complete.

Your implementation traded:

long frame

for:

incomplete frame

That is a dangerous trade in a renderer with persistent intermediate surfaces.

⸻

Why that explains the image retention

The next part of your renderer makes the failure substantially worse.

A number of your attachments intentionally preserve previous contents.

For example your normal depth target does:

depth_attachment.loadOp =
    depth_initialized
        ? VK_ATTACHMENT_LOAD_OP_LOAD
        : VK_ATTACHMENT_LOAD_OP_CLEAR;

Your resolve-conversion path similarly does:

color_attachment.loadOp =
    destination.layout == VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED
        ? VK_ATTACHMENT_LOAD_OP_DONT_CARE
        : VK_ATTACHMENT_LOAD_OP_LOAD;

And your native surface objects have persistent state such as:

ever_written

This makes sense because GTA IV performs lots of partial rendering, blending, post-processing and surface reuse.

But combine that with skipping draws:

frame N
surface contains complete scene A
frame N+1
new PSO required
↓
several important draws return fail("pipeline")
↓
surface LOADs previous contents
↓
only the draws whose PSOs already exist overwrite it
↓
transparent/post-FX draws blend over leftover scene A

Visually:

old camera image
      +
partially rendered current image
      +
translucent/post-FX composition

That is almost exactly the faint “previous frame sitting underneath the current frame” artifact you showed.

It also explains why it may linger longer than a single frame: a missing opaque draw does not necessarily overwrite the pixels left by the prior frame, and subsequent translucent/post-processing passes can preserve or transform those pixels.

Vulkan’s synchronization model does not invent clean attachment contents for you; applications are responsible for resource state and ordering.  

⸻

The completely black gameplay screen fits too

The black frame you described — gameplay/audio continuing but the entire rendered output black — makes the async PSO path even more suspicious.

If a new scene requires many previously unseen pipelines, the first several frames may look like:

opaque world pipeline A → compiling → SKIP
opaque world pipeline B → compiling → SKIP
vehicle pipeline → compiling → SKIP
terrain pipeline → compiling → SKIP
character pipeline → compiling → SKIP
lighting/composite pipeline already cached → executes
present → succeeds

From Vulkan’s perspective that is a perfectly successful rendered/presented frame.

It just contains almost no actual game geometry.

This is also consistent with the earlier Metal HUD observation:

~1.6 ms GPU
very high FPS
black output

A black screen with exceptionally low GPU time is exactly what I would expect from not submitting most of the game’s draws, rather than from a GPU hang.

The Khronos guidance for pipeline hitching recommends pipeline caches and creating known pipelines early. It warns about draw-time pipeline creation because of frame-time spikes; it does not suggest dropping the requested rendering work as the default solution.  

MoltenVK likewise recommends persistent Vulkan pipeline caching so SPIR-V→MSL/Metal shader work does not happen during gameplay.  

⸻

I no longer think FIF=2 is the primary cause

The two-frames-in-flight implementation still deserves auditing. Vulkan’s own tutorial states that any resource that is accessed and modified during rendering must be duplicated or otherwise synchronized when multiple frames are active.  

Your implementation duplicated:

command pool
command buffer
upload buffer
upload descriptor set
frame descriptor pool

That’s good.

But the actual native render surfaces remain globally shared:

native_surface_images_
native_texture_images_
post-FX surfaces
reflection resources
resolved resources
surface layout state
ever_written
placement ownership

Therefore FIF could still expose cross-frame hazards.

UnleashedRecomp is much more deliberate about per-frame scheduling:

g_frame = g_nextFrame;
g_nextFrame = (g_frame + 1) % NUM_FRAMES;
if (g_commandListStates[g_frame])
{
    g_queue->waitForCommandFence(
        g_commandFences[g_frame].get());
}
g_uploadAllocators[g_frame].reset();

Its command lists, upload allocators, query pools, semaphores and fences are indexed by g_frame.

Khronos specifically recommends mutating per-frame resources only after the associated frame fence is known complete.  

But FIF does not explain your symptoms as neatly as the pipeline change does, because:

1. Rendering eventually became visible again without removing FIF.
2. The corruption appeared in the same build that introduced “skip until ready.”
3. You have explicit fail("pipeline") paths.
4. You preserve attachment content via LOAD.
5. The completely black frames coincided with extremely cheap GPU frames.
6. UnleashedRecomp conspicuously avoids this strategy.

So I’d rank the suspects:

Suspect	Confidence
Async PSO → skipped draws + preserved surfaces	Very high
FIF=2 + globally shared mutable render surfaces	High
8 MiB streaming budget/null-texture fallback	Medium
Incorrect final present/swapchain reuse	Lower
GTA IV’s own motion blur/post processing	Essentially ruled out

The texture budget has another semantic problem

The second newly introduced optimization also intentionally renders incomplete frames:

if (deferred_texture_generations_.contains(
        texture->generation)) {
    return nullptr;
}

The comment confirms:

// Deferred by this frame's streaming upload budget;
// the draw samples the null texture until a later
// frame admits the payload.

Again, that changes rendering correctness in exchange for frame pacing.

UnleashedRecomp’s approach to streaming is much closer to:

upload resource
transition resource
bind resource
draw

rather than:

resource expensive this frame
→ silently substitute null
→ hope next frame looks correct

That optimization can explain black/untextured objects or transient pop-in. I don’t think it’s the main source of whole-frame retention, but it should not be considered a correctness-preserving optimization.

Khronos’ newer streaming example uses a transfer queue and timeline synchronization so graphics waits for resources that are actually ready, rather than silently changing what the draw samples.  

What I would change architecturally

The UnleashedRecomp comparison points to the right model:

                PSO discovered
                     │
            ┌────────┴─────────┐
            │                  │
      background/prewarm   render needs it
            │                  │
            ▼                  ▼
        compile early     cache lookup
                               │
                     ┌─────────┴────────┐
                     │                  │
                   found             missing
                     │                  │
                    draw         compile synchronously
                                  (correct but slow)

Not:

pipeline missing
      ↓
compile asynchronously
      ↓
SKIP THE DRAW
      ↓
present incomplete frame

The first model preserves correctness. Once your cache/prewarming gets good enough, the synchronous fallback should become uncommon.

There is another potentially useful Vulkan mechanism, VK_PIPELINE_CREATE_FAIL_ON_PIPELINE_COMPILE_REQUIRED_BIT, which can be used to detect whether an operation would require compilation. Vulkan explicitly returns VK_PIPELINE_COMPILE_REQUIRED in that case.   That can support a proper prewarm strategy, but it still shouldn’t mean “discard gameplay rendering.”

My conclusion

The optimization session introduced two semantic shortcuts that UnleashedRecomp does not rely on for normal rendering:

missing PSO     → skip draw
upload > budget → substitute null texture

The first is almost tailor-made to produce your image-retention bug because your renderer heavily relies on persistent render targets and LOAD semantics.

I would revert only those two correctness-changing behaviors first, retain the pipeline compiler infrastructure/cache, retain FIF=2 for now, and change async PSOs to precompile + synchronous miss fallback. Then run the exact same scene.

If the ghosting vanishes, we’ve isolated it without throwing away the 130 FPS gain from the rest of the work.

The FIF resource ownership problem should then be audited independently because your global render surfaces are still not truly frame-local, and Vulkan requires explicit handling for resources modified across overlapping frames.  Yeah — and that distinction matters.

If your renderer already has most GTA IV shaders dumped/precompiled, then the hitch is probably not raw shader compilation in the usual “SPIR-V source is being generated for the first time” sense. The expensive object being created at runtime is the graphics pipeline / PSO, which is a combination of much more than just the shader modules.

A single precompiled vertex/pixel shader pair can still require many different Vulkan pipelines because the pipeline key also includes things like blend mode, depth test/write state, stencil state, cull mode, primitive topology, MSAA sample count, render-target formats, depth format, vertex declaration, alpha-test specialization, primitive restart, and so on.

So conceptually:

Precompiled shaders:
VS_A
PS_B

can still turn into:

Pipeline 1 = VS_A + PS_B + opaque + depth-write + LESS + RT format A
Pipeline 2 = VS_A + PS_B + alpha blend + no depth-write + RT format A
Pipeline 3 = VS_A + PS_B + additive blend + depth-write + RT format B
Pipeline 4 = VS_A + PS_B + stencil Equal + RT format A
...

And your current renderer calls vkCreateGraphicsPipelines() when one of those exact combinations is missing.

That also changes how I read the UnleashedRecomp comparison. They aren’t merely “precompiling shaders.” They have machinery for precompiling pipeline states too. Their PipelineState includes shader pointers plus the fixed-function state:

vertexShader
pixelShader
vertexDeclaration
zEnable
zWriteEnable
srcBlend
destBlend
cullMode
zFunc
alphaBlendEnable
blendOp
depthBias
srcBlendAlpha
destBlendAlpha
colorWriteEnable
primitiveTopology
renderTargetFormat
depthStencilFormat
sampleCount
specConstants

Then they hash the whole thing:

XXH64_hash_t hash =
    XXH3_64bits(&pipelineState,
                sizeof(pipelineState));

and asynchronously compile that PSO ahead of rendering.

So if you’ve dumped most game shaders, that’s actually very useful: we may already have enough static knowledge to do something much closer to UnleashedRecomp and prebuild a huge fraction of the PSO space without ever skipping a gameplay draw.

The key question is what exactly your dump contains. If it’s only something like:

shader hash
SPIR-V
vertex inputs
specialization mask

then it tells us which shader programs exist, but not all the pipeline combinations GTA IV will use.

If you’ve also dumped runtime records containing:

VS hash
PS hash
vertex declaration
blend state
depth/stencil state
render-target formats
MSAA
topology
alpha specialization

then you’ve effectively dumped the game’s observed PSO set, and we can prewarm those directly.

Given how instrumented your renderer already is, I strongly suspect you may have enough data to reconstruct that set.

So I would revise my previous recommendation slightly:

Don’t abandon async PSO compilation. Your existing shader dump makes it potentially much better.

What I would abandon is this behavior:

if (pipeline_is_compiling)
    skip_draw();

Instead:

startup / loading screen
        ↓
load dumped shader metadata
        ↓
load known PSO-state database
        ↓
compile PSOs on worker threads
        ↓
gameplay
        ↓
PSO hit → draw immediately
PSO unexpected miss → synchronous compile once
                        + record PSO for next launch

That gives you a self-improving PSO cache.

And this is probably especially practical for GTA IV because the renderer already hashes shader/state combinations. After a few representative runs, the number of genuinely novel pipelines appearing during gameplay should fall sharply.

So yes: having most shaders dumped makes the current “skip the draw” implementation even less justified, because you’re in a good position to prewarm the actual PSOs instead.

The next useful thing would be for me to inspect your shader dump/cache code and determine exactly what you’ve already captured—shader modules only, or enough state to generate complete PSOs.

    #ifndef REX_GRAPHICS_GTA4_NATIVE_NATIVE_STREAMING_BUDGET_H_
    #define REX_GRAPHICS_GTA4_NATIVE_NATIVE_STREAMING_BUDGET_H_
    
    #include <cstdint>
    
    namespace rex::graphics::gta4_native {
    
    // Streaming texture uploads are amortized across frames: a frame admits
    // payloads until the budget is exhausted, and the remaining textures are
    // deferred to following frames (their draws sample the null texture for the
    // deferred frames). The first payload offered each frame is always admitted so
    // upload progress is guaranteed even when a single payload exceeds the whole
    // budget; callers must therefore offer the most critical payload (the present
    // source) first.
    class NativeUploadBudgetPlanner {
     public:
      // budget_bytes of zero disables budgeting entirely.
      void Reset(uint64_t budget_bytes) {
        budget_bytes_ = budget_bytes;
        admitted_bytes_ = 0;
        admitted_any_ = false;
      }
    
      bool Admit(uint64_t payload_bytes) {
        if (!budget_bytes_) {
          return true;
        }
        if (admitted_any_ && admitted_bytes_ + payload_bytes > budget_bytes_) {
          return false;
        }
        admitted_any_ = true;
        admitted_bytes_ += payload_bytes;
        return true;
      }
    
      uint64_t admitted_bytes() const { return admitted_bytes_; }
    
     private:
      uint64_t budget_bytes_ = 0;
      uint64_t admitted_bytes_ = 0;
      bool admitted_any_ = false;
    };
    
    }  // namespace rex::graphics::gta4_native
    
    #endif  // REX_GRAPHICS_GTA4_NATIVE_NATIVE_STREAMING_BUDGET_H_

    TEST_CASE("GTA IV upload budget admits until the budget is exhausted") {
      gta4::NativeUploadBudgetPlanner planner;
      planner.Reset(1000);
      REQUIRE(planner.Admit(400));
      REQUIRE(planner.Admit(600));
      REQUIRE_FALSE(planner.Admit(1));
      REQUIRE(planner.admitted_bytes() == 1000);
    }
    
    TEST_CASE("GTA IV upload budget always admits the first payload") {
      gta4::NativeUploadBudgetPlanner planner;
      planner.Reset(64);
      // A payload larger than the whole budget still uploads when it is first,
      // guaranteeing forward progress (and protecting the present source, which
      // callers offer first).
      REQUIRE(planner.Admit(1 << 20));
      // The oversized first admission consumes the frame's budget entirely.
      REQUIRE_FALSE(planner.Admit(1));
    }
    
    TEST_CASE("GTA IV upload budget zero disables budgeting") {
      gta4::NativeUploadBudgetPlanner planner;
      planner.Reset(0);
      for (int i = 0; i < 64; ++i) {
        REQUIRE(planner.Admit(uint64_t(1) << 30));
      }
    }
    
    TEST_CASE("GTA IV upload budget resets between frames") {
      gta4::NativeUploadBudgetPlanner planner;
      planner.Reset(100);
      REQUIRE(planner.Admit(100));
      REQUIRE_FALSE(planner.Admit(50));
      planner.Reset(100);
      REQUIRE(planner.Admit(50));
      REQUIRE(planner.Admit(50));
      REQUIRE_FALSE(planner.Admit(1));
    }

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import re
    from collections import Counter, defaultdict
    from pathlib import Path
    
    log_dir = Path("out/build/macos-release/LibertyRecomp/Liberty Recompiled.app/Contents/MacOS/logs")
    paths = sorted(log_dir.glob("Liberty Recompiled_528*.log"))
    gbuffer = Counter()
    scene = Counter()
    scene_zero = defaultdict(list)
    queries = defaultdict(lambda: Counter())
    
    for path in paths:
        for line in path.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines():
            match = re.search(r"point=translucent-query-recorded frame=(\d+) cmd=(\d+).*category=(gbuffer-write|scene-write)", line)
            if match:
                frame = int(match.group(1))
                category = match.group(3)
                if "variant=original" in line:
                    (gbuffer if category == "gbuffer-write" else scene)[frame] += 1
            match = re.search(r"point=translucent-query-result frame=(\d+) cmd=(\d+).*category=(gbuffer-write|scene-write) variant=([^ ]+).*samples-passed=(\d+)", line)
            if match:
                frame = int(match.group(1))
                category = match.group(3)
                variant = match.group(4)
                passed = int(match.group(5))
                queries[(frame, category, variant)][passed] += 1
            match = re.search(r"point=depth-lifecycle-value frame=(\d+) cmd=(\d+).*category=scene-resolve.*nonzero=(\d+)/(\d+)", line)
            if match:
                scene_zero[int(match.group(1))].append((int(match.group(2)), int(match.group(3)), int(match.group(4))))
    
    frames = sorted(set(gbuffer) | set(scene) | set(scene_zero))
    print("frame gbuffer_draws scene_draws scene_resolves(nonzero/total) gbuffer_raster scene_original")
    for frame in frames:
        raster = queries.get((frame, "gbuffer-write", "raster-only"), {})
        original = queries.get((frame, "scene-write", "original"), {})
        resolve = ",".join(f"{cmd}:{nonzero}/{total}" for cmd, nonzero, total in scene_zero.get(frame, [])) or "-"
        print(frame, gbuffer[frame], scene[frame], resolve, dict(raster), dict(original))

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import struct
    
    
    def rgb565(value):
        red = ((value >> 11) & 31) / 31.0
        green = ((value >> 5) & 63) / 63.0
        blue = (value & 31) / 31.0
        return red, green, blue
    
    
    def block_mean(block):
        color0, color1, selectors = struct.unpack("<HHI", block)
        palette = [rgb565(color0), rgb565(color1)]
        if color0 > color1:
            palette += [
                tuple((2.0 * a + b) / 3.0 for a, b in zip(palette[0], palette[1])),
                tuple((a + 2.0 * b) / 3.0 for a, b in zip(palette[0], palette[1])),
            ]
        else:
            palette += [tuple((a + b) / 2.0 for a, b in zip(palette[0], palette[1])), (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)]
        pixels = [palette[(selectors >> (pixel * 2)) & 3] for pixel in range(16)]
        return tuple(sum(pixel[channel] for pixel in pixels) / 16.0 for channel in range(3))
    
    
    red = struct.pack("<HHI", 0xF800, 0, 0)
    black = bytes(8)
    assert block_mean(red) == (1.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    assert block_mean(black) == (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    print("BC1 probe decoder reference cases passed")

    import glob

        r"point=texture-payload-audit frame=(\d+) cmd=(\d+).*"
        r"payload-bytes=(\d+) nonzero-bytes=(\d+) complete-blocks=(\d+) "
        r"nonzero-blocks=(\d+)"
    )
    shadow_re = re.compile(
        r"stage=(main-scene-(?:selected-sample|all-host-samples)-resolve).*"
        r"nonzero=(\d+)/(\d+).*checksum=([0-9A-F]+)"
    )
    query_re = re.compile(
        r"point=translucent-query-result frame=(\d+) cmd=(\d+).*"
        r"category=gbuffer-write variant=([^ ]+).*samples-passed=(\d+)"
    )
    geometry_re = re.compile(
        r"point=gbuffer-indexed-geometry frame=(\d+) cmd=(\d+).*"
        r"count=(\d+) range=(\d+)\.\.(\d+) .*indexed-positions=\[(.*)\]"
    )

    queries = defaultdict(dict)

        with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as source:
            for line in source:
                match = payload_re.search(line)
                if match:

                        int(value) for value in match.groups()
                    )
                    payloads.append(
                        (frame, command, payload_bytes, nonzero_bytes, blocks,
                         nonzero_blocks, blocks * 8 == payload_bytes)

                match = query_re.search(line)

                    queries[(int(frame), int(command))][variant] = int(passed)
                match = geometry_re.search(line)

    #include <cstdint>
    #include <fstream>
    #include <iostream>
    #include <string>
    #include <vector>
    
    #include "smolv.h"
    
    int main(int argc, char** argv) {
      if (argc != 5) {
        std::cerr << "usage: decode_gta4_smolv CACHE OFFSET SIZE OUTPUT\n";
        return 2;
      }
      const std::string cache_path = argv[1];
      const uint64_t offset = std::stoull(argv[2]);
      const uint64_t size = std::stoull(argv[3]);
      std::ifstream input(cache_path, std::ios::binary | std::ios::ate);
      if (!input) return 3;
      const uint64_t cache_size = static_cast<uint64_t>(input.tellg());
      if (offset > cache_size || size > cache_size - offset) return 4;
      std::vector<uint8_t> encoded(size);
      input.seekg(static_cast<std::streamoff>(offset));
      input.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(encoded.data()),
                 static_cast<std::streamsize>(size));
      const size_t decoded_size = smolv::GetDecodedBufferSize(encoded.data(), encoded.size());
      if (!decoded_size || decoded_size % sizeof(uint32_t)) return 5;
      std::vector<uint8_t> decoded(decoded_size);
      if (!smolv::Decode(encoded.data(), encoded.size(), decoded.data(), decoded.size())) return 6;
      std::ofstream output(argv[4], std::ios::binary);
      output.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(decoded.data()),
                   static_cast<std::streamsize>(decoded.size()));
      std::cout << "offset=" << offset << " encoded=" << size
                << " decoded=" << decoded_size << "\n";
      return output ? 0 : 7;
    }

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import pathlib
    import re
    import subprocess
    
    source = pathlib.Path("LibertyRecompLib/shader/shader_cache.cpp")
    text = source.read_text()
    match = re.search(
        r"const uint8_t g_compressedSpirvCache\[\] = \{([^}]*)\};",
        text,
        re.S,
    )
    if not match:
        raise SystemExit("compressed SPIR-V cache array not found")
    values = [int(value) for value in re.findall(r"\d+", match.group(1))]
    compressed = pathlib.Path("/tmp/gta4_spirv_cache.zst")
    decompressed = pathlib.Path("/tmp/gta4_spirv_cache.smolv")
    compressed.write_bytes(bytes(values))
    subprocess.run(
        ["/opt/homebrew/bin/zstd", "-d", "-f", str(compressed), "-o", str(decompressed)],
        check=True,
    )
    print(f"compressed_bytes={len(values)} decompressed_bytes={decompressed.stat().st_size}")

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import glob
    import math
    import re
    import struct
    import sys
    
    
    def f32(word):
        return struct.unpack("!f", bytes.fromhex(word))[0]
    
    
    paths = []
    for pattern in sys.argv[1:]:
        paths.extend(glob.glob(pattern))
    
    vs_records = {}
    geometry_records = {}
    for path in sorted(set(paths)):
        with open(path, errors="replace") as stream:
            for line in stream:
                if "point=gbuffer-vs-inputs" in line:
                    key_match = re.search(r"frame=(\d+) cmd=(\d+).*vs=([0-9A-F]+)", line)
                    if not key_match:
                        continue
                    constants = {}
                    for register, body in re.findall(r"c(\d+)=\[([^]]+)\]", line):
                        constants[int(register)] = [
                            f32(word)
                            for word in re.findall(r"([0-9A-F]{8}):", body)
                        ]
                    target_match = re.search(r"target=(\d+)x(\d+)", line)
                    vs_records[(int(key_match.group(1)), int(key_match.group(2)))] = {
                        "vs": key_match.group(3),
                        "constants": constants,
                        "width": int(target_match.group(1)),
                        "height": int(target_match.group(2)),
                    }
                elif "point=gbuffer-indexed-geometry" in line:
                    key_match = re.search(r"frame=(\d+) cmd=(\d+)", line)
                    if not key_match:
                        continue
                    positions = []
                    for _, body in re.findall(r"i\d+=v(\d+)\[([^]]+)\]", line):
                        positions.append([
                            f32(word)
                            for word in re.findall(r"([0-9A-F]{8}):", body)
                        ])
                    geometry_records.setdefault(
                        (int(key_match.group(1)), int(key_match.group(2))), positions
                    )
    
    for key in sorted(set(vs_records) & set(geometry_records)):
        record = vs_records[key]
        constants = record["constants"]
        if not all(register in constants for register in (8, 9, 10, 11)):
            continue
        print(f"frame={key[0]} cmd={key[1]} vs={record['vs']}")
        rows = [constants[register] for register in (8, 9, 10, 11)]
        for ordinal, position in enumerate(geometry_records[key]):
            x, y, z = position
            raw = [
                x * rows[0][component]
                + y * rows[1][component]
                + z * rows[2][component]
                + rows[3][component]
                for component in range(4)
            ]
            adjusted = list(raw)
            adjusted[0] += raw[3] / record["width"]
            adjusted[1] -= raw[3] / record["height"]
            adjusted[1] = -adjusted[1]
            finite = all(math.isfinite(value) for value in adjusted)

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import glob
    import hashlib
    import math
    import pathlib
    import re
    import struct
    import sys
    
    
    VERTEX_CONSTANTS_OFFSET = 0x780
    TARGET_WIDTH = 3456
    TARGET_HEIGHT = 2168
    
    
    def sha256(path):
        digest = hashlib.sha256()
        with open(path, "rb") as stream:
            for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
                digest.update(block)
        return digest.hexdigest()
    
    
    def read_constant(snapshot, register):
        offset = VERTEX_CONSTANTS_OFFSET + register * 16
        return struct.unpack_from(">4f", snapshot, offset)
    
    
    def transform(position, rows):
        x, y, z = position
        raw = [
            x * rows[0][component]
            + y * rows[1][component]
            + z * rows[2][component]
            + rows[3][component]
            for component in range(4)
        ]
        raw[0] += raw[3] / TARGET_WIDTH
        raw[1] -= raw[3] / TARGET_HEIGHT
        raw[1] = -raw[1]
        return tuple(raw)
    
    
    def clip_polygon(polygon):
        planes = (
            lambda v: v[3] + v[0],
            lambda v: v[3] - v[0],
            lambda v: v[3] + v[1],
            lambda v: v[3] - v[1],
            lambda v: v[2],
            lambda v: v[3] - v[2],
        )
        for plane in planes:
            if not polygon:
                return []
            output = []
            previous = polygon[-1]
            previous_distance = plane(previous)
            for current in polygon:
                current_distance = plane(current)
                previous_inside = previous_distance >= 0.0
                current_inside = current_distance >= 0.0
                if previous_inside != current_inside:
                    denominator = previous_distance - current_distance
                    if denominator:
                        t = previous_distance / denominator
                        output.append(
                            tuple(
                                previous[component]
                                + t * (current[component] - previous[component])
                                for component in range(4)
                            )
                        )
                if current_inside:
                    output.append(current)
                previous = current
                previous_distance = current_distance
            polygon = output
        return polygon
    
    
    def ndc_area(vertices):
        ndc = [(v[0] / v[3], v[1] / v[3]) for v in vertices]
        return abs(
            (ndc[1][0] - ndc[0][0]) * (ndc[2][1] - ndc[0][1])
            - (ndc[1][1] - ndc[0][1]) * (ndc[2][0] - ndc[0][0])
        )
    
    
    records = []
    for pattern in sys.argv[1:]:
        for log_path in glob.glob(pattern):
            with open(log_path, errors="replace") as stream:
                for line in stream:
                    if "point=gbuffer-geometry-artifact" not in line:
                        continue
                    fields = dict(re.findall(r"([a-z][a-z0-9-]*)=([^ ]+)", line))
                    if fields.get("result") == "written":
                        records.append(fields)
    
    seen = set()
    for fields in records:
        vertex_path = pathlib.Path(fields["vertex-path"])
        if vertex_path in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(vertex_path)
        host_index_path = pathlib.Path(fields["host-index-path"])
        guest_index_path = pathlib.Path(fields["guest-index-path"])
        snapshot_path = pathlib.Path(fields["snapshot-path"])
        vertex_data = vertex_path.read_bytes()
        index_data = host_index_path.read_bytes()
        snapshot = snapshot_path.read_bytes()
        index32 = fields["index32"] == "true"
        index_format = "<I" if index32 else "<H"
        index_size = struct.calcsize(index_format)
        indices = [
            struct.unpack_from(index_format, index_data, offset)[0]
            for offset in range(0, len(index_data), index_size)
        ]
        base_vertex = int(fields["base"])
        stride = int(fields["stride"])
        stream_offset = int(fields["stream-offset"])
        position_offset = int(fields["position-offset"])
        components = int(fields["components"])
        rows = [read_constant(snapshot, register) for register in (8, 9, 10, 11)]
    
        positions = {}
        clips = {}
        out_of_bounds = []
        for index in sorted(set(indices)):
            adjusted_index = index + base_vertex
            offset = stream_offset + adjusted_index * stride + position_offset
            required = offset + components * 4
            if adjusted_index < 0 or offset < 0 or required > len(vertex_data):
                out_of_bounds.append(index)
                continue
            values = list(struct.unpack_from(">" + "f" * components, vertex_data, offset))
            while len(values) < 3:
                values.append(0.0)
            position = tuple(values[:3])
            positions[index] = position
            clips[index] = transform(position, rows)
    
        finite = [clip for clip in clips.values() if all(math.isfinite(v) for v in clip)]
        inside_xy = [
            clip
            for clip in finite
            if clip[3] > 0.0 and abs(clip[0]) <= clip[3] and abs(clip[1]) <= clip[3]
        ]
        inside_z = [
            clip for clip in finite if clip[3] > 0.0 and 0.0 <= clip[2] <= clip[3]
        ]
        fully_inside = [
            clip
            for clip in finite
            if clip[3] > 0.0
            and abs(clip[0]) <= clip[3]
            and abs(clip[1]) <= clip[3]
            and 0.0 <= clip[2] <= clip[3]
        ]
    
        triangles_total = len(indices) // 3
        triangles_finite = 0
        triangles_surviving_clip = 0
        triangles_non_degenerate = 0
        for triangle_index in range(triangles_total):
            triangle_indices = indices[triangle_index * 3 : triangle_index * 3 + 3]
            if any(index not in clips for index in triangle_indices):
                continue
            triangle = [clips[index] for index in triangle_indices]
            if not all(math.isfinite(value) for vertex in triangle for value in vertex):
                continue
            triangles_finite += 1
            clipped = clip_polygon(triangle)
            if clipped:
                triangles_surviving_clip += 1
            if all(vertex[3] != 0.0 for vertex in triangle) and ndc_area(triangle) > 0.0:
                triangles_non_degenerate += 1
    
        def bounds(component):
            values = [clip[component] for clip in finite]
            return (min(values), max(values)) if values else (math.nan, math.nan)
    
        ndc_values = [
            (clip[0] / clip[3], clip[1] / clip[3], clip[2] / clip[3])
            for clip in finite
            if clip[3] != 0.0
        ]
        ndc_bounds = [
            (min(v[c] for v in ndc_values), max(v[c] for v in ndc_values))
            if ndc_values
            else (math.nan, math.nan)
            for c in range(3)
        ]
    
        print(
            f"frame={fields['frame']} cmd={fields['cmd']} vs={fields['vs']} "
            f"indices={len(indices)} unique={len(set(indices))} decoded={len(clips)} "
            f"oob={len(out_of_bounds)} finite={len(finite)} inside_xy={len(inside_xy)} "
            f"inside_z={len(inside_z)} fully_inside={len(fully_inside)}"
        )
        print(
            f"  triangles total={triangles_total} finite={triangles_finite} "
            f"surviving_clip={triangles_surviving_clip} "
            f"non_degenerate_preclip={triangles_non_degenerate}"
        )
        print(
            f"  clip_bounds x={bounds(0)} y={bounds(1)} z={bounds(2)} w={bounds(3)} "
            f"ndc_bounds x={ndc_bounds[0]} y={ndc_bounds[1]} z={ndc_bounds[2]}"
        )
        print(
            f"  sha256 vertex={sha256(vertex_path)} "
            f"index_guest={sha256(guest_index_path)} "
            f"index_host={sha256(host_index_path)} snapshot={sha256(snapshot_path)}"
        )

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import glob
    import re
    import sys
    
    
    TARGETS = {"4D629CC41AD0FE18", "43005295B40E2DB6"}
    draws = {}
    results = []
    
    for pattern in sys.argv[1:]:
        for path in glob.glob(pattern, recursive=True):
            try:
                stream = open(path, errors="replace")
            except OSError:
                continue
            with stream:
                for line_number, line in enumerate(stream, 1):
                    if "point=draw-state" in line:
                        match = re.search(
                            r"frame=(\d+).*draw-id=([0-9A-F]+).*vs=[^: ]*:([0-9A-F]+).*"
                            r"constants=([0-9A-F]+):([0-9A-F]+)",
                            line,
                        )
                        if match and match.group(3) in TARGETS:
                            key = (path, int(match.group(1)), match.group(2))
                            draws[key] = {
                                "path": path,
                                "line": line_number,
                                "frame": int(match.group(1)),
                                "draw": match.group(2),
                                "vs": match.group(3),
                                "vc": match.group(4),
                                "pc": match.group(5),
                            }
                    elif "point=translucent-query-result" in line:
                        match = re.search(
                            r"frame=(\d+).*draw=([0-9A-F]+).*category=([^ ]+).*"
                            r"variant=([^ ]+).*result=(\d+)",
                            line,
                        )
                        if match:
                            results.append(
                                (
                                    path,
                                    int(match.group(1)),
                                    match.group(2),
                                    match.group(3),
                                    match.group(4),
                                    int(match.group(5)),
                                    line_number,
                                )
                            )
    
    joined = []
    for path, frame, draw, category, variant, result, line_number in results:
        record = draws.get((path, frame, draw))
        if record:
            joined.append((record, category, variant, result, line_number))
    
    print(f"target_draws={len(draws)} joined_results={len(joined)}")
    for record, category, variant, result, result_line in sorted(
        joined,
        key=lambda item: (
            item[3] == 0,
            item[0]["path"],
            item[0]["frame"],
            item[0]["draw"],
            item[2],
        ),
    ):
        print(
            f"result={result} variant={variant} category={category} "
            f"vs={record['vs']} vc={record['vc']} pc={record['pc']} "
            f"frame={record['frame']} draw={record['draw']} "
            f"source={record['path']}:{record['line']} result-line={result_line}"
        )

    Add: /tmp/compare_gbuffer_constant_upload.py
    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import hashlib
    import pathlib
    import sys
    
    
    SNAPSHOT_CONSTANT_OFFSET = 0x780
    CONSTANT_BYTES = 0x1000
    
    
    def digest(data: bytes) -> str:
        return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
    
    
    def guest_words_to_host(data: bytes) -> bytes:
        if len(data) % 4:
            raise ValueError(f"constant block size is not word aligned: {len(data)}")
        return b"".join(data[offset : offset + 4][::-1]
                        for offset in range(0, len(data), 4))
    
    
    def main() -> int:
        if len(sys.argv) != 3:
            raise SystemExit("usage: compare_gbuffer_constant_upload.py SNAPSHOT HOST_UPLOAD")
        snapshot_path = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
        upload_path = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[2])
        snapshot = snapshot_path.read_bytes()
        upload = upload_path.read_bytes()
        guest = snapshot[SNAPSHOT_CONSTANT_OFFSET:
                         SNAPSHOT_CONSTANT_OFFSET + CONSTANT_BYTES]
        converted = guest_words_to_host(guest)
        mismatches = [index for index, pair in enumerate(zip(converted, upload))
                      if pair[0] != pair[1]]
        print(f"snapshot={snapshot_path}")
        print(f"upload={upload_path}")
        print(f"snapshot_bytes={len(snapshot)} guest_constant_bytes={len(guest)} "
              f"upload_bytes={len(upload)}")
        print(f"guest_sha256={digest(guest)}")
        print(f"converted_sha256={digest(converted)}")
        print(f"upload_sha256={digest(upload)}")
        print(f"exact={converted == upload} mismatch_bytes={len(mismatches)}")
        if mismatches:
            for index in mismatches[:16]:
                print(f"mismatch offset=0x{index:X} expected=0x{converted[index]:02X} "
                      f"actual=0x{upload[index]:02X}")
        return 0 if converted == upload else 1
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        raise SystemExit(main())

    Add: /tmp/analyze_native_frame.py
    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import argparse
    import collections
    import re
    from pathlib import Path
    
    
    def field(line: str, name: str):
        match = re.search(rf"(?:^| )({re.escape(name)})=([^ ]+)", line)
        return match.group(2) if match else None
    
    
    def main():
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("log", type=Path)
        parser.add_argument("frame", type=int)
        args = parser.parse_args()
    
        marker = f"frame={args.frame}"
        lines = [line.rstrip() for line in args.log.read_text(errors="replace").splitlines()
                 if marker in line]
        draws = [line for line in lines if "point=draw-state" in line]
        results = [line for line in lines if "point=command-result" in line and "type=draw" in line]
        queries = [line for line in lines if "point=translucent-query-result" in line]
        checkpoints = [line for line in lines if "scene-checkpoint" in line]
    
        target_counts = collections.Counter()
        depth_counts = collections.Counter()
        pair_counts = collections.Counter()
        for line in draws:
            target = field(line, "rt") or "missing"
            depth = field(line, "depth") or "missing"
            target_handle = target.split(":", 2)[0]
            depth_handle = depth.split(":", 2)[0]
            target_counts[target_handle] += 1
            depth_counts[depth_handle] += 1
            pair_counts[(target_handle, depth_handle)] += 1
    
        print(f"frame={args.frame} matching_lines={len(lines)} draw_states={len(draws)} "
              f"draw_results={len(results)} query_results={len(queries)} "
              f"checkpoints={len(checkpoints)}")
        print("target_counts")
        for key, value in target_counts.most_common():
            print(f"  {key} {value}")
        print("depth_counts")
        for key, value in depth_counts.most_common():
            print(f"  {key} {value}")
        print("target_depth_pairs")
        for (target, depth), value in pair_counts.most_common():
            print(f"  {target} {depth} {value}")
    
        print("main_gbuffer_draws")
        for line in draws:
            target = field(line, "rt") or ""
            depth = field(line, "depth") or ""
            if target.startswith("40226720:") or depth.startswith("40226690:"):
                print("  " + line.split("] ", 4)[-1])
    
        print("scene_queries")
        for line in queries:
            category = field(line, "category")
            if category in {"gbuffer-write", "scene-write", "water-surface",
                            "vehicle-glass", "vehicle-light", "light-sprite"}:
                print("  " + line.split("] ", 4)[-1])
    
        print("checkpoints")
        for line in checkpoints:
            print("  " + line.split("] ", 4)[-1])
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import collections
    import glob
    import re
    import sys
    
    
    FIELD = re.compile(r"([a-z][a-z0-9-]*)=([^ ]+)")
    
    
    def parse_int(value):
        if value is None:
            return None
        return int(value, 0)
    
    
    def main():
        if len(sys.argv) != 2:
            raise SystemExit("usage: analyze_command_boundaries.py 'glob'")
        records = []
        for path in glob.glob(sys.argv[1]):
            with open(path, errors="replace") as stream:
                for line_number, line in enumerate(stream, 1):
                    if "point=command-frame-boundary" not in line:
                        continue
                    fields = dict(FIELD.findall(line))
                    fields["path"] = path
                    fields["line"] = line_number
                    for name in (
                        "frame", "epoch", "boundary-sequence", "queued-after",
                        "commands", "draws", "main-gbuffer-draws",
                        "scene-phase-draws", "resolves", "clears", "handoffs",
                        "epoch-mismatches"):
                        fields[name] = parse_int(fields.get(name))
                    records.append(fields)
    
        records.sort(key=lambda item: item["boundary-sequence"])
        by_epoch = collections.defaultdict(list)
        for record in records:
            by_epoch[record["epoch"]].append(record)
    
        flush_records = [record for record in records
                         if record.get("boundary") == "texture-lock-flush"]
        present_records = [record for record in records
                           if record.get("boundary") == "present"]
        split_epochs = [epoch for epoch, items in by_epoch.items()
                        if any(item.get("boundary") == "texture-lock-flush" for item in items)
                        and any(item.get("boundary") == "present" for item in items)]
    
        print(f"records={len(records)} presents={len(present_records)} "
              f"texture_lock_flushes={len(flush_records)} "
              f"split_epochs={len(split_epochs)}")
        print("split_epoch_details")
        for epoch in split_epochs:
            for record in by_epoch[epoch]:
                print(
                    f"  epoch={epoch} boundary={record['boundary']} "
                    f"frame={record['frame']} sequence={record['boundary-sequence']} "
                    f"queued_after={record['queued-after']} "
                    f"commands={record['commands']} draws={record['draws']} "
                    f"main_gbuffer={record['main-gbuffer-draws']} "
                    f"scene_phase={record['scene-phase-draws']} "
                    f"resolves={record['resolves']} clears={record['clears']} "
                    f"handoffs={record['handoffs']} "
                    f"epoch_mismatches={record['epoch-mismatches']} "
                    f"source={record['path']}:{record['line']}")
    
        print("largest_present_batches")
        for record in sorted(present_records, key=lambda item: item["draws"],
                             reverse=True)[:20]:
            print(
                f"  frame={record['frame']} epoch={record['epoch']} "
                f"commands={record['commands']} draws={record['draws']} "
                f"main_gbuffer={record['main-gbuffer-draws']} "
                f"scene_phase={record['scene-phase-draws']} "
                f"sequence={record['boundary-sequence']} "
                f"source={record['path']}:{record['line']}")
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import argparse
    import collections
    import glob
    import re
    
    
    def field(line, name):
        match = re.search(rf"(?:^| ){re.escape(name)}=([^ ]+)", line)
        return match.group(1) if match else None
    
    
    def main():
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("log_glob")
        parser.add_argument("frame", type=int)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        marker = f"frame={args.frame}"
        lines = []
        for path in glob.glob(args.log_glob):
            with open(path, errors="replace") as stream:
                lines.extend(line.rstrip() for line in stream if marker in line)
        draws = [line for line in lines if "point=draw-state" in line]
        target_counts = collections.Counter()
        depth_counts = collections.Counter()
        pair_counts = collections.Counter()
        for line in draws:
            target = (field(line, "rt") or "missing").split(":", 1)[0]
            depth = (field(line, "depth") or "missing").split(":", 1)[0]
            target_counts[target] += 1
            depth_counts[depth] += 1
            pair_counts[(target, depth)] += 1
        print(f"frame={args.frame} matching_lines={len(lines)} draw_states={len(draws)}")
        print("target_counts")
        for key, value in target_counts.most_common():
            print(f"  {key} {value}")
        print("depth_counts")
        for key, value in depth_counts.most_common():
            print(f"  {key} {value}")
        print("target_depth_pairs")
        for (target, depth), value in pair_counts.most_common():
            print(f"  {target} {depth} {value}")
    
    
    if __name__ == "__main__":
        main()

    #pragma once
    
    namespace rex::graphics::gta4_native {
    
    // The title deliberately switches from multisampled deferred attachments to
    // single-sampled persistent/forward attachments. A host MSAA quality override
    // may change the sample count of the former, but must never promote the latter:
    // doing so changes the depth/stencil handoff topology and invalidates the
    // title-authored stencil contents used by the scene composite.
    constexpr bool ShouldApplyNativeSceneSampleOverride(
        bool reflection_target, bool has_bound_surface,
        bool all_bound_surfaces_are_guest_multisampled) {
      return !reflection_target && has_bound_surface &&
             all_bound_surfaces_are_guest_multisampled;
    }
    
    }  // namespace rex::graphics::gta4_native

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import glob
    import json
    import re
    
    paths = glob.glob(
        "/Users/Ozordi/Downloads/LibertyRecomp/out/build/macos-release/"

    handoff_ok = 0
    handoff_destination_samples = []
    original_passes = {}
    scene_composite_passes = 0
    validation_errors = 0
    
    surface_pattern = re.compile(
        r"created (?:color|depth) surface ([0-9A-F]{8}).* samples (\d+)"
    )
    handoff_pattern = re.compile(
        r"point=explicit-depth-handoff .*result=ok .*destination-samples=(\d+)"
    )
    query_pattern = re.compile(
        r"point=translucent-query-result .*category=([^ ]+) variant=original .*"
        r"ps=([0-9A-F]+).*samples-passed=(\d+)"
    )

            for line in stream:
                surface_match = surface_pattern.search(line)
                if surface_match:
                    surface_samples.setdefault(surface_match.group(1), set()).add(
                        int(surface_match.group(2))
                    )
                handoff_match = handoff_pattern.search(line)
                if handoff_match:
                    handoff_ok += 1
                    handoff_destination_samples.append(int(handoff_match.group(1)))
                query_match = query_pattern.search(line)
                if query_match and int(query_match.group(3)) > 0:
                    category = query_match.group(1)
                    original_passes[category] = original_passes.get(category, 0) + 1
                    if query_match.group(2) == "7B14CAC2A31D4199":
                        scene_composite_passes += 1
                if re.search(
                    r"VUID-|Validation Error|VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST|device lost",
                    line,
                    re.IGNORECASE,
                ):
                    validation_errors += 1
    
    result = {
        "files": len(paths),
        "surface_samples": {
            handle: sorted(samples) for handle, samples in sorted(surface_samples.items())
        },
        "handoff_ok": handoff_ok,
        "handoff_destination_samples": sorted(set(handoff_destination_samples)),
        "scene_composite_passes": scene_composite_passes,
        "original_passes": dict(sorted(original_passes.items())),
        "validation_errors": validation_errors,
    }
    
    assert result["surface_samples"].get("40226690") == [2]
    assert result["surface_samples"].get("400007C0") == [1]
    assert result["surface_samples"].get("40076EB0") == [1]

    assert scene_composite_passes > 0
    assert original_passes.get("water-surface", 0) > 0
    assert original_passes.get("vehicle-glass", 0) > 0
    assert validation_errors == 0

    +// VkSampleCountFlagBits values are the corresponding power-of-two sample
    +// counts. Select the requested count when supported, otherwise the greatest
    +// coherent lower count. Returning zero means even the mandatory 1x fallback
    +// was not advertised and surface creation must fail explicitly.
    +constexpr uint32_t SelectSupportedNativeSceneSampleCount(
    +    uint32_t requested, uint32_t supported) {
    +  if (requested >= 4u && (supported & 4u)) {
    +    return 4u;
    +  }
    +  if (requested >= 2u && (supported & 2u)) {
    +    return 2u;
    +  }
    +  return supported & 1u;
    +}
    +
     }  // namespace rex::graphics::gta4_native

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    import glob
    import re
    import sys
    
    paths = sys.argv[1:] or glob.glob(
        "out/build/macos-release/LibertyRecomp/Liberty Recompiled.app/Contents/MacOS/logs/Liberty Recompiled_55*.log"
    )
    registration_re = re.compile(
        r"host registration family=(\d+) role=(\d+).*wrapper=([0-9A-F]+) surface=([0-9A-F]+) texture=([0-9A-F]+)"
    )
    surface_re = re.compile(
        r"created (?:color|depth) surface ([0-9A-F]+).*reflection=(true|false) family=(\d+) role=(\d+)"
    )
    present_re = re.compile(r"present(?:=|.*source=)([0-9A-F]{8})")
    
    registrations = {}
    events = []
    for path in paths:
        with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as stream:
            for line_number, line in enumerate(stream, 1):
                match = registration_re.search(line)
                if match:
                    family, role, wrapper, surface, texture = match.groups()
                    record = (path, line_number, family, role, wrapper, surface, texture)
                    for handle in (surface, texture):
                        if handle != "00000000":
                            registrations.setdefault(handle, []).append(record)
                    events.append((path, line_number, "registration", surface, texture, family, role))
                    continue
                match = surface_re.search(line)
                if match:
                    handle, reflection, family, role = match.groups()
                    if handle in registrations:
                        events.append((path, line_number, "surface", handle, reflection, family, role))
                match = present_re.search(line)
                if match and match.group(1) in registrations:
                    events.append((path, line_number, "present", match.group(1)))
    
    print(f"files={len(paths)} registered_handles={len(registrations)} joined_events={len(events)}")
    for event in events:
        print("|".join(map(str, event)))

    #ifndef REX_GRAPHICS_GTA4_NATIVE_NATIVE_REFLECTION_REGISTRY_H_
    #define REX_GRAPHICS_GTA4_NATIVE_NATIVE_REFLECTION_REGISTRY_H_
    
    #include <cstddef>
    #include <cstdint>
    #include <unordered_map>
    
    #include <rex/graphics/gta4_native/title_commands.h>
    
    namespace rex::graphics::gta4_native {
    
    struct NativeReflectionTarget {
      ReflectionFamily family = ReflectionFamily::kMirror;
      ReflectionRole role = ReflectionRole::kColor;
      uint32_t wrapper = 0;
      uint32_t surface = 0;
      uint32_t texture = 0;
      uint32_t logical_width = 0;
      uint32_t logical_height = 0;
      uint32_t physical_width = 0;
      uint32_t physical_height = 0;
      uint32_t sample_count_override = 0;
    };
    
    using NativeReflectionRegistry =
        std::unordered_map<uint32_t, NativeReflectionTarget>;
    
    inline bool SameNativeReflectionRegistration(
        const NativeReflectionTarget& left,
        const NativeReflectionTarget& right) {
      return left.family == right.family && left.role == right.role &&
             left.wrapper == right.wrapper && left.surface == right.surface &&
             left.texture == right.texture;
    }
    
    // A color reflection is exposed through an attachment surface and a sampled
    // texture. Releasing either member retires both aliases. Keeping the other raw
    // handle alive can misclassify a later title resource that reuses it.
    inline size_t EraseNativeReflectionRegistration(
        NativeReflectionRegistry& registry, uint32_t resource) {
      const auto matched = registry.find(resource);
      if (matched == registry.end()) {
        return 0;
      }
      const NativeReflectionTarget registration = matched->second;
      return std::erase_if(registry, [&registration](const auto& entry) {
        return SameNativeReflectionRegistration(entry.second, registration);
      });
    }
    
    inline size_t RegisterNativeReflectionTarget(
        NativeReflectionRegistry& registry,
        const NativeReflectionTarget& registration) {
      size_t retired_aliases =
          EraseNativeReflectionRegistration(registry, registration.surface);
      if (registration.texture) {
        retired_aliases +=
            EraseNativeReflectionRegistration(registry, registration.texture);
      }
      registry[registration.surface] = registration;
      if (registration.texture) {
        registry[registration.texture] = registration;
      }
      return retired_aliases;
    }
    
    inline const NativeReflectionTarget* FindNativeReflectionSurface(
        const NativeReflectionRegistry& registry,
        const SurfaceDescriptor& descriptor, bool depth) {
      const auto entry = registry.find(descriptor.handle);
      if (entry == registry.end()) {
        return nullptr;
      }
      const NativeReflectionTarget& registration = entry->second;
      const ReflectionRole requested_role =
          depth ? ReflectionRole::kDepth : ReflectionRole::kColor;
      if (registration.surface != descriptor.handle ||
          registration.role != requested_role ||
          registration.logical_width != descriptor.width ||
          registration.logical_height != descriptor.height) {
        return nullptr;
      }
      return &registration;
    }
    
    inline const NativeReflectionTarget* FindNativeReflectionTexture(
        const NativeReflectionRegistry& registry, uint32_t handle,
        uint32_t logical_width, uint32_t logical_height) {
      const auto entry = registry.find(handle);
      if (entry == registry.end()) {
        return nullptr;
      }
      const NativeReflectionTarget& registration = entry->second;
      if (registration.role != ReflectionRole::kColor ||
          registration.texture != handle ||
          registration.logical_width != logical_width ||
          registration.logical_height != logical_height) {
        return nullptr;
      }
      return &registration;
    }
    
    }  // namespace rex::graphics::gta4_native
    
    #endif  // REX_GRAPHICS_GTA4_NATIVE_NATIVE_REFLECTION_REGISTRY_H_

    #include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>
    
    #include "graphics/gta4_native/native_reflection_registry.h"
    
    namespace rex::graphics::gta4_native {
    namespace {
    
    NativeReflectionTarget MakeWaterColorRegistration() {
      NativeReflectionTarget target{};
      target.family = ReflectionFamily::kWater;
      target.role = ReflectionRole::kColor;
      target.wrapper = 0x1000;
      target.surface = 0x2000;
      target.texture = 0x3000;
      target.logical_width = 320;
      target.logical_height = 180;
      target.physical_width = 1920;
      target.physical_height = 1080;
      return target;
    }
    
    TEST_CASE("GTA IV native reflection release retires paired aliases") {
      NativeReflectionRegistry registry;
      const NativeReflectionTarget target = MakeWaterColorRegistration();
      CHECK(RegisterNativeReflectionTarget(registry, target) == 0);
      CHECK(registry.size() == 2);
    
      CHECK(EraseNativeReflectionRegistration(registry, target.surface) == 2);
      CHECK(registry.empty());
    
      RegisterNativeReflectionTarget(registry, target);
      CHECK(EraseNativeReflectionRegistration(registry, target.texture) == 2);
      CHECK(registry.empty());
    }
    
    TEST_CASE("GTA IV native reflection registration replaces colliding identity") {
      NativeReflectionRegistry registry;
      const NativeReflectionTarget water = MakeWaterColorRegistration();
      RegisterNativeReflectionTarget(registry, water);
    
      NativeReflectionTarget replacement = water;
      replacement.family = ReflectionFamily::kMirror;
      replacement.wrapper = 0x4000;
      replacement.texture = 0x5000;
      CHECK(RegisterNativeReflectionTarget(registry, replacement) == 2);
      CHECK_FALSE(registry.contains(water.texture));
      CHECK(registry.contains(replacement.surface));
      CHECK(registry.contains(replacement.texture));
    }
    
    TEST_CASE("GTA IV native reflection lookup validates role and logical extent") {
      NativeReflectionRegistry registry;
      const NativeReflectionTarget target = MakeWaterColorRegistration();
      RegisterNativeReflectionTarget(registry, target);
    
      SurfaceDescriptor surface{};
      surface.handle = target.surface;
      surface.width = target.logical_width;
      surface.height = target.logical_height;
      CHECK(FindNativeReflectionSurface(registry, surface, false) != nullptr);
      CHECK(FindNativeReflectionSurface(registry, surface, true) == nullptr);
    
      surface.width = 3456;
      surface.height = 2168;
      CHECK(FindNativeReflectionSurface(registry, surface, false) == nullptr);
    
      CHECK(FindNativeReflectionTexture(registry, target.texture,
                                        target.logical_width,
                                        target.logical_height) != nullptr);
      CHECK(FindNativeReflectionTexture(registry, target.texture, 3456, 2168) ==
            nullptr);
      CHECK(FindNativeReflectionTexture(registry, target.surface,
                                        target.logical_width,
                                        target.logical_height) == nullptr);
    }
    
    }  // namespace
    }  // namespace rex::graphics::gta4_native

    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    from pathlib import Path
    import re
    
    log_dir = Path("out/build/macos-release/LibertyRecomp/Liberty Recompiled.app/Contents/MacOS/logs")
    paths = sorted(log_dir.glob("Liberty Recompiled_554*.log"))
    text = "\n".join(path.read_text(errors="replace") for path in paths)
    
    host_registration = re.findall(
        r"host registration .*?role=(\d+).*?logical=(\d+)x(\d+).*?physical=(\d+)x(\d+).*?surface=([0-9A-F]+) texture=([0-9A-F]+).*?retired-aliases=(\d+)",
        text,
    )
    created_primary = re.findall(
        r"created color surface ([0-9A-F]+) guest=(\d+)x(\d+) host=(\d+)x(\d+).*?reflection=(\w+)",
        text,
    )
    errors = re.findall(
        r"VUID-|Validation Error|device lost|Device lost|result=rejected|target reject|resolve fail",
        text,
        flags=re.IGNORECASE,
    )
    
    print(f"files={len(paths)}")
    print(f"host_registrations={len(host_registration)}")
    print(f"created_color_surfaces={len(created_primary)}")
    print(f"validation_or_device_errors={len(errors)}")
    for item in host_registration:
        print("registration=" + ":".join(item))
    for item in created_primary[:8]:
        print("surface=" + ":".join(item))
    
    assert paths
    assert host_registration
    assert not errors

## Assistant

Fixed and rebuilt.

The bug was not render order—the trace proved reflections finish before HUD/menu draws. The real issue was stale reflection aliases: releasing a reflection surface or texture left its paired handle registered, so reused handles could be misclassified as high-resolution reflections and contaminate UI rendering.

Changes:

- Reflection surface/texture aliases now retire together.
- Reflection routing validates exact surface-vs-texture role and logical dimensions.
- Stale aliases can no longer classify full-size HUD/frontbuffer resources as reflections.
- Added deterministic lifecycle and handle-reuse tests.

## Assistant

I found the precise steering defect in the title-side injector: GTA stores each action as an encoded pair, `effective = byte0 XOR byte2`. The injector compared and wrote raw `byte2`, so any negative-polarity action (including one steering direction) can decode to zero or the wrong magnitude. That bug exists only because the second path bypasses the controller pipeline. I’m removing that post-processed action mutation and making keyboard/mouse produce one complete XInput state before GTA processes it; then I’ll lock the mapping and neutral-state behavior with focused tests.
